M04-body-P078.title: Only for those who have attained jhāna

paragraphs.M04-body-P078-S01: If you have developed the skeleton or foulness subject to absorption, apprehend the mentality of first jhāna on the skeleton attended to as repulsive, and on the foulness subject, as in the first-jhāna row of the attainment tables with the breathing or kasiṇa counterpart sign. The tables above suffice for apprehending the mentality called jhāna phenomena.
paragraphs.M04-body-P078-S02:
Lābhino eva pana mahaggatacittāni supākaṭāni honti.
Exalted consciousnesses are very evident only to those who have attained them. (Mahāṭīkā, vol. 2, p. 353.) Thus only those who have attained jhāna apprehend and discern its mentality. Pure-insight practitioners without jhāna leave this part aside.
paragraphs.M04-body-P078-S03: Both those who have apprehended jhāna mentality and pure-insight practitioners without jhāna should continue with sense-sphere mentality. As the Visuddhimagga says, “Evaṃ chasu dvāresu arūpassa nibbatti passitabbā”, apprehend and discern so that wisdom sees the arising of mentality at the six doors. (Vol. 2, p. 253.)

M04-body-P079.title: Process abbreviations and beginning to apprehend jhāna

paragraphs.M04-body-P079-S01: Names of the process consciousnesses in the tables above:
paragraphs.M04-body-P079-S02:
M — mind-door adverting: adverts to or determines the jhāna object, such as the breathing counterpart sign.
P — preparation (parikamma): a great wholesome sense-sphere impulsion preparing for jhāna impulsion.
U — access (upacāra): a great wholesome impulsion arising close to jhāna impulsion.
A — conformity (anuloma): a great wholesome impulsion conforming to the arising of jhāna impulsion.
G — change-of-lineage (gotrabhū): a great wholesome impulsion crossing out of the sense-sphere lineage.
J — jhāna impulsion: fine-material or immaterial wholesome impulsion.
paragraphs.M04-body-P079-S03: When apprehending the mentality in the first-jhāna attainment process shown above, meditators know the impulsions occurring in the modes of preparation, access, conformity and change-of-lineage, rather than knowing the conventional names. For worldlings and trainees, those impulsions…

paragraphs.M04-body-P080-S01: … are great wholesome impulsions. For arahants they are great functional impulsions. In one of keen understanding there are just three access impulsions: access, conformity and change-of-lineage.
paragraphs.M04-body-P080-S02: A beginner in meditation on mentality who wishes to apprehend jhāna mentality should enter the jhāna to be apprehended. After emerging, apprehend together the clear life-continuum mind-door and the jhāna object, such as the breathing counterpart sign. Begin with the jhāna factors. Repeat the exercise many times. When the tranquillity sign, such as the breathing counterpart sign, appears at the life-continuum mind-door, use wisdom to see, apprehend and distinguish the factors arising together in each successive jhāna impulsion moment. Once successful through repetition, one may begin with knowing consciousness, feeling, or contact.
paragraphs.M04-body-P080-S03: Choose one of the three ways and increase the number one mental phenomenon at a time until all the jhāna factors and associated phenomena are apprehended with wisdom in each moment. First enter jhāna and, as soon as you emerge, practise seeing one jhāna mental phenomenon over many moments. Enter again and on emerging practise seeing two over many moments. Continue entering and emerging in this way…

M04-body-P081.title: Thirty-four first-jhāna mental phenomena with the breathing counterpart sign

paragraphs.M04-body-P081-S01: … increasing by one jhāna mental phenomenon at a time. Those with a strong grounding in Abhidhamma and keen understanding may apprehend them this way. Those with less grounding and slower understanding can find it very difficult to grasp their nature. For their sake the 34 first-jhāna mental phenomena that arise taking the breathing counterpart sign as object are set out again below.
paragraphs.M04-body-P081-S02: The group of factors such as applied thought is called jhāna. The consciousness and mental factors associated with it are called phenomena associated with jhāna. Discern the jhāna and the associated phenomena by characteristic, function, manifestation and proximate cause (Visuddhimagga, vol. 2, p. 222).
paragraphs.M04-body-P081-S03: 1. Knowing consciousness (citta) — apprehending the breathing counterpart sign as object. “Vijānanaṃ ārammaṇassa upaladdhi” (Mūlaṭīkā, vol. 1, p. 87).
paragraphs.M04-body-P081-S04:
2. Contact (phassa) — has the characteristic of touching the breathing counterpart sign. Its function is to connect knowing consciousness with that object.
Note: “object” for the mental factors listed below also means the breathing counterpart sign.

M04-body-P082.title: First-jhāna mental phenomena from feeling to joy

paragraphs.M04-body-P082-S01:
3. Feeling (vedanā) — experiencing the flavour of the object pleasantly and gladly. In first jhāna this is joyful feeling (somanassavedanā).
4. Perception (saññā) — marking the object.
5. Volition (cetanā) — prompting and urging the associated phenomena towards the object.
6. One-pointedness (ekaggatā) — the mind resting on one object, standing firm and keeping the associated phenomena from scattering.
7. Life faculty (jīvita) — maintaining the associated phenomena.
8. Attention (manasikāra) — directing and driving the mind and associated phenomena towards the object, bringing the object to mind.
paragraphs.M04-body-P082-S02:
9. Applied thought (vitakka) — placing the mind and associated phenomena on the object, also having the nature of thinking.
10. Sustained thought (vicāra) — repeatedly examining, rubbing against and taking hold of the object.
11. Decision (adhimokkha) — deciding with respect to the object.
12. Energy (viriya) — striving to know the object, that is, for the associated phenomena to arise, and supporting them in reaching the object.
13. Joy (pīti) — delighting in the object.

M04-body-P083.title: First-jhāna mental phenomena from desire to lightness of the mental body

paragraphs.M04-body-P083-S01:
14. Desire (chanda) — wishing to know the object, that is, wishing the associated phenomena to arise.
15. Faith (saddhā) — confidence in the practice of jhāna concentration.
16. Mindfulness (sati) — making associated phenomena sink into the object like a stone instead of floating like a gourd. It does not forget the object and keeps the mind on it.
17. Moral shame (hiri) — shame at evil, unwholesome phenomena and misconduct.
18. Moral dread (ottappa) — fear of evil, unwholesome phenomena and misconduct.
paragraphs.M04-body-P083-S02:
19. Non-greed (alobha) — not clinging or being attached to the object, and not appropriating it as “mine”.
20. Non-hatred (adosa) — the mind is neither harsh nor fierce towards the object and does not wish to destroy it.
21. Specific neutrality (tatramajjhattatā) — keeping the mind balanced on the meditation object so it neither becomes elated through conceit nor sinks through sloth and torpor. It remains equanimous towards the object.
22. Tranquillity of the mental body (kāyapassaddhi) — the mental factors are tranquil on the object.
23. Tranquillity of consciousness (cittapassaddhi) — consciousness is tranquil on the object.
24. Lightness of the mental body (kāyalahutā) — the mental factors are quick and light on the object.

M04-body-P084.title: First-jhāna mental phenomena from lightness of consciousness to wisdom

paragraphs.M04-body-P084-S01:
25. Lightness of consciousness (cittalahutā) — consciousness is quick and light on the object.
26. Malleability of the mental body (kāyamudutā) — the mental factors are pliant on the object.
27. Malleability of consciousness (cittamudutā) — consciousness is pliant on the object.
28. Wieldiness of the mental body (kāyakammaññatā) — the mental factors are workable, suitable and serviceable on the object.
29. Wieldiness of consciousness (cittakammaññatā) — consciousness is workable, suitable and serviceable on the object.
paragraphs.M04-body-P084-S02:
30. Proficiency of the mental body (kāyapāguññatā) — the mental factors are adept, readily trained and free of the sickness of defilements.
31. Proficiency of consciousness (cittapāguññatā) — consciousness is adept, readily trained and free of the sickness of defilements.
32. Rectitude of the mental body (kāyujukatā) — the mental factors are straight on the object, free from deceit and duplicity.
33. Rectitude of consciousness (cittujukatā) — consciousness is straight on the object, free from deceit and duplicity.
34. Wisdom (paññā) — penetrating the breathing counterpart sign as object.
paragraphs.M04-body-P084-S03: Note: The twelve mental phenomena at mind-door adverting are consciousness and the mental factors from knowing consciousness through energy in the list of thirty-four above.

paragraphs.M04-body-P085-S01: Jhāna mental phenomena generally take a counterpart sign as object, with some exceptions. In mindfulness of breathing, jhāna and its associated mental phenomena take the breathing counterpart sign. In attention to the repulsiveness of bones they take the bone counterpart sign. In the white kasiṇa (odāta) they take the white kasiṇa counterpart sign. In loving-kindness the object is a being as a concept. In foulness meditation the object is the counterpart sign of a foul corpse. If the meditator has developed and dwelt in jhāna with breathing, attention to the repulsiveness of bones, the white kasiṇa and the four protective meditations, the jhāna mental phenomena to apprehend and seek are as follows.
paragraphs.M04-body-P085-S02:
1. Breathing — first, second, third and fourth jhānas.
2. Attention to the repulsiveness of bones — first jhāna.
3. White kasiṇa — first, second, third and fourth jhānas.
4. Loving-kindness — first, second and third jhānas.
5. Foulness — first jhāna.
paragraphs.M04-body-P085-S03: If the good person has developed all ten kasiṇas and the attainments with each kasiṇa, all eight attainments are included among the objects discerned by insight knowledge. The immaterial jhānas…

M04-body-P086.title: How to begin apprehending first-jhāna mentality

paragraphs.M04-body-P086-S01: … each have thirty-one mental phenomena, the same number as fourth jhāna. Seek and apprehend them according to the fourth-jhāna table. Understand the other subjects similarly except compassion and appreciative joy. These two subjects can reach third jhāna. In compassion meditation, add the compassion factor to the breathing-jhāna mental phenomena. In appreciative-joy meditation, add the appreciative-joy factor. Thus the three levels have thirty-five, thirty-three and thirty-two mental phenomena respectively.
paragraphs.M04-body-P086-S02: Seek and apprehend the jhāna mental phenomena as shown in the tables. In the impulsions leading to second jhāna and higher levels, namely preparation, access, conformity and change-of-lineage, applied and sustained thought are still associated (Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 2, p. 237). In the access moments for fourth jhāna, joy too is absent (Visuddhimagga, vol. 1, p. 160).
paragraphs.M04-body-P086-S03: To seek and apprehend the first-jhāna mental phenomena of breathing, first enter the first jhāna of breathing. After emerging, begin by apprehending its factors. Practise seeing them arise many times in uninterrupted succession. If the ability is still weak, take the breathing counterpart sign as object and enter first jhāna again. On emerging:
paragraphs.M04-body-P086-S04:
1. Apprehend the clear life-continuum, the mind-door.
2. Direct attention to and apprehend the breathing counterpart sign.
3. When that sign appears in the clear life-continuum, the mind-door, apprehend and seek the jhāna factors again.

M04-body-P087.title: Gradually increasing the number of mental phenomena apprehended

paragraphs.M04-body-P087-S01: Just after emerging from jhāna, the breathing counterpart sign remains and does not readily disappear. By repeatedly training in this method, apprehending the base and object together with jhāna mentality, meditators gradually learn to seek and apprehend many occurrences of the jhāna factors. This is an ancient instruction that Venerable Sāriputta, the General of the Dhamma, followed with care.
paragraphs.M04-body-P087-S02: First return to first jhāna with the breathing counterpart sign. Then begin apprehending jhāna mentality from knowing consciousness, or from feeling or contact. If you start from consciousness, practise seeing just knowing consciousness arise many times in succession. Starting from feeling or contact works similarly. Once successful, enter jhāna again. As soon as you emerge, practise seeing with wisdom repeated pairs of knowing consciousness and contact. When successful, enter again. On emerging, apprehend repeated groups of three: knowing consciousness, contact and feeling. Then take groups of four by adding perception, groups of five by adding volition, and continue increasing one phenomenon at a time.
paragraphs.M04-body-P087-S03: Finally, practise seeing with wisdom the twelve mental phenomena at the moment of mind-door adverting and thirty-four at each impulsion moment, occurring many times in succession. Enter jhāna repeatedly and add one mental phenomenon to apprehend each time you emerge. When successful…

M04-body-P088.title: Delimiting mentality and a note on the sixteen phenomena

paragraphs.M04-body-P088-S01:
Pariggahetvā sabbampetaṃ ārammaṇābhimukhaṃ namanato namanaṭṭhena nāmanti vavatthapeti.
Having apprehended it, one determines all this as mentality in the sense of bending, because it inclines towards the object (Visuddhimagga, vol. 2, p. 222).
paragraphs.M04-body-P088-S02: When you discern with wisdom the twelve mental phenomena at mind-door adverting and the thirty-four arising together at each moment of preparation, access, conformity, change-of-lineage and jhāna impulsion, occurring in repeated succession, see that they all turn and incline towards the same object, the breathing counterpart sign. Because they incline towards the object, distinguish and apprehend them as mentality, mental phenomena.
paragraphs.M04-body-P088-S03: Note: Alternate repeatedly between entering jhāna and apprehending its mental phenomena. They are clear to wisdom immediately after emergence. Remember to re-enter when they are indistinct.
paragraphs.M04-body-P088-S04: Points to note. In the Anupada Sutta, when Venerable Sāriputta apprehended the first-jhāna mental phenomena for insight, the Pāli names sixteen directly: applied thought, sustained thought, joy, pleasure, one-pointedness, contact, feeling, perception, volition, consciousness, desire, decision, energy, mindfulness, equanimity (specific neutrality), and attention. The commentary also says “soḷasa dhammā”, sixteen phenomena (Majjhima Commentary, vol. 4, p. 60), and explains that he apprehended them by their individual characteristics. However, the teacher known as Ācariya Dhammapāla…

M04-body-P089.title: Two interpretations of the mental phenomena named in the Anupada Sutta

paragraphs.M04-body-P089-S01: … distinguishes two interpretations, the elders’ interpretation and a further interpretation, as follows (Majjhima Subcommentary, vol. 3, p. 277).
paragraphs.M04-body-P089-S02: Soḷasannaṃ eva cettha dhammānaṃ gahaṇaṃ tesaṃyeva therena vavatthāpitabhāvato, te evassa tadā upaṭṭhahiṃsu, na itareti vadanti. Vīriyasatiggahaṇena cettha indriyabhāvasāmaññato saddhāpaññā, satiggahaṇeneva ekantānavajjabhāvasāmaññato passaddhiādayo cha yugaḷā, alobhādosā ca saṅgahitā jhānacittuppādapariyāpannattā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ. Therena ca dhammā vavatthānasāmaññato āraddhā. Te na upaṭṭhahiṃsūti na sakkā vattunti apare.
paragraphs.M04-body-P089-S03: The elders’ interpretation. The discourse directly teaches and singles out sixteen jhāna-associated phenomena because Venerable Sāriputta distinguished each of those sixteen by wisdom. At that time those sixteen phenomena were clear and established in his knowing wisdom. The other phenomena associated with jhāna were indistinct, according to these teachers.
paragraphs.M04-body-P089-S04: The further interpretation. Among the first-jhāna mental phenomena, energy and mindfulness serve as faculties called the energy faculty and the mindfulness faculty. Naming energy and mindfulness directly thus includes and teaches faith and wisdom, which also serve as faculties. The life faculty is understood similarly. Mindfulness is associated only with beautiful consciousness and is wholly faultless. In expressly teaching faultless mindfulness…

M04-body-P090.title: Phenomena included in the further interpretation

paragraphs.M04-body-P090-S01: … the teaching also includes and teaches the entirely faultless mental factors of the same nature. These are the six pairs: tranquillity of the mental body and of consciousness, lightness of each, malleability of each, wieldiness of each, proficiency of each, and rectitude of each, as well as non-greed and non-hatred. These phenomena are all included in the arising of jhāna consciousness. Venerable Sāriputta also distinguished the phenomena associated with jhāna individually by their own characteristics and developed insight. Therefore the teachers of the further interpretation say it is inappropriate to claim that the jhāna-associated phenomena outside the sixteen were indistinct to his knowing wisdom (Majjhima Subcommentary, vol. 3, p. 277).
paragraphs.M04-body-P090-S02:
Yo yo aṭṭhakathāvādo vā theravādo vā pacchā vuccati, so pamāṇato daṭṭhabbo.
Whichever interpretation of the commentary or the elders is stated last should be regarded as authoritative (Vinaya Commentary, vol. 1, p. 260).
paragraphs.M04-body-P090-S03: Under this convention of exposition (Vinaya Commentary, vol. 1, p. 260), the subcommentator placed the further interpretation last for the reader to take as the authoritative conclusion. It also accords with discourses that give an open-ended exposition. After apprehending the mental phenomena in a jhāna attainment in this way, the next stage of practice…

paragraphs.M04-body-P091-S01: … is described in the Visuddhimagga as follows.
paragraphs.M04-body-P091-S02:
Tato yathā nāma puriso antogehe sappaṃ disvā taṃ anubandhamāno tassa āsayaṃ passati, evameva ayampi yogāvacaro taṃ nāmaṃ upaparikkhanto “idaṃ nāmaṃ kiṃ nissāya pavattatī”ti pariyesamāno tassa nissayaṃ hadayarūpaṃ passati. Tato hadayarūpassa nissayabhūtāni, bhūtanissitāni ca sesupādāyarūpānīti rūpaṃ pariggaṇhāti. So sabbampetaṃ ruppanato rūpanti vavatthapeti. Tato namanalakkhaṇaṃ nāmaṃ, ruppanalakkhaṇaṃ rūpanti saṅkhepato nāmarūpaṃ vavatthapeti.
Visuddhimagga, vol. 2, p. 222.
paragraphs.M04-body-P091-S03: After apprehending jhāna mentality, the meditator is like a person who sees a snake in a house and follows it to its dwelling. The meditator investigates with wisdom, “Depending on what does this mentality occur?” In seeking, the meditator sees the heart-base materiality on which mentality depends. Then the meditator uses wisdom to distinguish and apprehend the four great elements supporting the heart-base and the other derived materiality that depends on those elements. Owing to their susceptibility to alteration, the meditator determines all these phenomena to be materiality. Then…

M04-body-P092.title: From jhāna mentality to mentality that takes materiality as object

paragraphs.M04-body-P092-S01:
1. What has the characteristic of inclining towards an object is mentality.
2. What has the characteristic of being altered is materiality.
One thus distinguishes mentality and materiality in brief (Visuddhimagga, vol. 2, p. 222).
paragraphs.M04-body-P092-S02: Following the commentary above, after apprehending jhāna mentality, apprehend the fifty-four instances of elemental and derived materiality in the heart on which jhāna mentality depends, and distinguish materiality and mentality. When apprehending sense-sphere mentality in the eye-door process and the other five-door and mind-door processes, likewise apprehend the materiality at the relevant door on which those mental phenomena depend, then distinguish mentality and materiality. See the materiality tables for elemental and derived materiality at the six doors.
paragraphs.M04-body-P092-S03: After apprehending the jhāna mental phenomena in the domain of mind objects, the meditator proceeds to apprehend mentality arising with materiality as object. By object, materiality is classified under six headings: visible form, sound, odour, taste, tangible object and mind object. Among these, it is easier to begin with the bare mind-door process taking the five sensitivities and sixteen subtle material phenomena that are mind objects, because fewer kinds of consciousness occur. Of the material phenomena classed as mind objects, eleven are concrete and ten non-concrete. Since a male meditator cannot find femininity materiality in his own continuum, nor a female meditator masculinity materiality in hers, only ten concrete material phenomena in one’s own continuum serve as objects for…

paragraphs.M04-body-P093-S01: … the mental phenomena to be sought and apprehended. For practical purposes the material phenomena may be grouped where the practice is the same. The subcommentary also explains that this is a generalization for the hearer based on similarity of practice, without separate treatment of another person’s continuum (Majjhima Subcommentary, vol. 3, pp. 274–275). Apprehend mentality arising with each of those material phenomena as object. When mind-door adverting in these processes determines the object with wise attention, a bare mind-door process with wholesome impulsions arises. When it determines the object with unwise attention, a bare mind-door process with unwholesome impulsions arises. The two ways of attending are briefly explained below.
paragraphs.M04-body-P093-S02: Parasantānagate ca tesaṃ santānavibhāgaṃ akatvā bahiddhābhāvasāmaññato sammasanaṃ, ayaṃ sāvakānaṃ sammasanacāro.
paragraphs.M04-body-P093-S03:
So “idaṃ dukkhan”ti yoniso manasi karoti, “ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo”ti yoniso manasi karoti, “ayaṃ dukkhanirodho”ti yoniso manasi karoti, “ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā”ti yoniso manasi karoti.
Majjhima Nikāya, vol. 1, pp. 11–12.
paragraphs.M04-body-P093-S04:
Tattha katamo ayoniso manasikāro? “Anicce niccan”ti ayoniso manasikāro, “dukkhe sukhan”ti ayoniso manasikāro, “anattani attā”ti ayoniso manasikāro, “asubhe subhan”ti ayoniso manasikāro. Saccavippaṭikūlena vā cittassa āvaṭṭanā anāvaṭṭanā ābhogo samannāhāro manasikāro. Ayaṃ vuccati ayoniso manasikāro.
Abhidhamma, vol. 2, pp. 387–388.

M04-body-P094.title: Definition and four ways of attending wisely

paragraphs.M04-body-P094-S01:
Tattha yoniso manasikāro nāma upāyamanasikāro pathamanasikāro. Aniccādīsu aniccantiādināva nayena saccānulomikena vā cittassa āvaṭṭanā anāvaṭṭanā ābhogo samannāhāro manasikāro. Ayaṃ vuccati yoniso manasikāroti.
Majjhima Commentary, vol. 1, p. 66.
paragraphs.M04-body-P094-S02:
Ayoniso manasikāroti anupāyamanasikāro uppathamanasikāro. Anicce niccanti dukkhe sukhanti anattani attāti asubhe subhanti ayoniso manasikāro uppathamanasikāro. Saccavippaṭikūlena vā cittassa āvaṭṭanā anāvaṭṭanā ābhogo samannāhāro manasikāro. Ayaṃ vuccati ayoniso manasikāroti.
Majjhima Commentary, vol. 1, pp. 66–67.
paragraphs.M04-body-P094-S03:
Cittassa āvaṭṭanātiādīni sabbāni pi āvajjanasseva vevacanāni. Āvaṭṭanāti bhavaṅgaṃ āvaṭṭetīti cittassa āvaṭṭanā.
Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 2, p. 482.
paragraphs.M04-body-P094-S04: Wise attention attends by the proper means, on the proper path: “This is the noble truth of suffering”, “This is the noble truth of the origin of suffering”, “This is the noble truth of the cessation of suffering”, and “This is the noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering, to Nibbāna”. Attending in this way is called wise attention (Majjhima Nikāya, vol. 1, pp. 11–12).

M04-body-P095.title: Attention in accordance with and contrary to the Four Noble Truths

paragraphs.M04-body-P095-S01: Wise attention sets the object in mind and attends by the proper means and on the proper path, as a cause for the welfare and happiness of path, fruition and Nibbāna.
paragraphs.M04-body-P095-S02:
1. Attend to the five impermanent aggregates as impermanent.
2. Attend to the five suffering aggregates as suffering.
3. Attend to the five non-self aggregates as non-self.
4. Attend to the five unattractive aggregates as unattractive.
paragraphs.M04-body-P095-S03: Adverting in that way or in a manner consistent with the Four Noble Truths turns the life-continuum, redirects the mind rightly, brings an object to mind, turns properly towards an object other than that of the life-continuum, and sets that other object in mind. Adverting in this way is called wise attention (Majjhima Commentary, vol. 1, p. 66).
paragraphs.M04-body-P095-S04:
What is unwise attention?
1. Attending to the five impermanent aggregates as permanent.
2. Attending to the five suffering aggregates as pleasant.
3. Attending to the five non-self aggregates as self.
4. Attending to the five unattractive aggregates as attractive.
paragraphs.M04-body-P095-S05: That sets the object in mind in a way that does not lead to the welfare and happiness of path, fruition and Nibbāna. It attends by wrong means, on the wrong path. Further, adverting turns the life-continuum in a manner unfavourable to penetrating the Four Noble Truths…

M04-body-P096.title: Great wholesome mentality taking eye-sensitivity as object

paragraphs.M04-body-P096-S01: … redirects the mind wrongly, brings the object to mind, directs it to an object other than that of the life-continuum and places that other object in mind. Adverting by such wrong means and on such a wrong path is called unwise attention (Abhidhamma, vol. 2, pp. 387–388. Majjhima Commentary, vol. 1, pp. 66–67).
paragraphs.M04-body-P096-S02: As explained above, attending to ultimate mentality and materiality as materiality, mentality, cause, effect, impermanent, suffering, non-self or unattractive is wise attention. Attending to eye-sensitivity as eye-sensitivity, as materiality, impermanent, suffering, non-self or unattractive is also wise attention. Understand the same for all materiality and mentality.
paragraphs.M04-body-P096-S03:
Thirty-four great wholesome mental phenomena arise taking eye-sensitivity as object.
1. Knowing consciousness — apprehends eye-sensitivity as object.
2. Contact — touches eye-sensitivity and connects knowing consciousness with that object.
3. Feeling — experiences the flavour of the eye-sensitivity object…

M04-body-P097.title: Mental phenomena taking eye-sensitivity as object

paragraphs.M04-body-P097-S01:
… pleasantly (joyful feeling).
4. Perception — marks eye-sensitivity as object.
5. Volition — prompts and urges associated phenomena towards the object of eye-sensitivity.
6. One-pointedness — rests the mind on the single object of eye-sensitivity, keeps it steady and prevents the associated phenomena from scattering.
7. Life faculty — sustains the associated phenomena.
8. Attention — directs and drives the mind and associated phenomena towards eye-sensitivity, bringing that object to mind.
paragraphs.M04-body-P097-S02: This suffices to convey the meaning, so only selected mental factors are shown here. They differ from the thirty-four jhāna mental phenomena only in object. Their types are the same.
paragraphs.M04-body-P097-S03:
15. Faith — confidence in the training in wisdom that penetrates the eye-sensitivity object.
34. Wisdom — penetrates eye-sensitivity as object.
paragraphs.M04-body-P097-S04: This suffices to understand the mental phenomena arising with eye-sensitivity as object. For a good person who has thoroughly memorized the fifty-two mental factors…

M04-body-P098.title: Preparing to read the bare mind-door process table

paragraphs.M04-body-P098-S01: … together with their nature and meaning, this is not very difficult. Understand ear-sensitivity and the other concrete and non-concrete material phenomena similarly. Taking eye-sensitivity as an example, the following table presents the wholesome group of bare mind-door processes in the domain of mind objects. The “wholesome group” here means processes containing wholesome impulsions.

paragraphs.M04-body-P099-S01:
Bare mind-door processes taking mind objects. Supporting materiality in the heart: 54.
Way of knowing the object | Mind-door adverting | Impulsion (7 times) | Registration (2 times) | Four cases
1. As eye-sensitivity | 12 | 34 | 34 | With knowledge, with joy
 | 12 | 33 | 33 | With knowledge, without joy
 | 12 | 33 | 33 | Without knowledge, with joy
 | 12 | 32 | 32 | Without knowledge, without joy
2. As materiality | 12 | 34 (33 / 33 / 32) | 34 (33 / 33 / 32) | As in the four cases above
3. As impermanent | 12 | 34 (33 / 33 / 32) | 34 (33 / 33 / 32) | As in the four cases above
4. As suffering | 12 | 34 (33 / 33 / 32) | 34 (33 / 33 / 32) | As in the four cases above
5. As non-self | 12 | 34 (33 / 33 / 32) | 34 (33 / 33 / 32) | As in the four cases above
6. As unattractive | 12 | 34 (33 / 33 / 32) | 34 (33 / 33 / 32) | As in the four cases above

M04-body-P100.title: How to apprehend mind-door processes with wholesome impulsions

paragraphs.M04-body-P100-S01: Here the consciousness and mental factors that know “eye-sensitivity”, “materiality”, “impermanent”, “suffering”, “non-self” and “unattractive” are the mental phenomena being sought and apprehended.
paragraphs.M04-body-P100-S02: The table above shows twenty-four cases for apprehending mentality arising with eye-sensitivity as object. It is intended to show how wholesome impulsions occur when one attends wisely. In apprehending them, remember first to analyse material clusters until you penetrate eye-sensitivity as ultimate reality. Understand the same for all concrete and non-concrete materiality. The method is illustrated below with mind-door processes having wholesome impulsions and taking eye-sensitivity as object.
paragraphs.M04-body-P100-S03:
1. Re-establish a previously attained fourth-jhāna concentration or the highest concentration you favour.
2. Apprehend the clear life-continuum, the mind-door.

M04-body-P101.title: Six ways of attending wisely to eye-sensitivity

paragraphs.M04-body-P101-S01: 3. Direct the mind to ultimate eye-sensitivity. When that object appears before the clear life-continuum, the mind-door, series of mind-door processes with impulsion arise. Mind-door adverting in those series determines the object in the following ways.
paragraphs.M04-body-P101-S02:
1. Determine it as eye-sensitivity.
2. Determine eye-sensitivity as materiality.
3. Take its arising and passing away, its liability to break up, as object and discern it as impermanent.
4. Take its being continually oppressed by arising and passing away as object and discern it as suffering.
5. Take its lack of any permanent, enduring, indestructible self as object and discern it as non-self.
6. Take its repulsiveness due to being mixed with unattractive colours, smells and the like as object and discern it as unattractive.
paragraphs.M04-body-P101-S03: With correct attention, that is, wise attention, wholesome impulsions arise. Of these six ways, begin by apprehending the series of mind-door processes with impulsion that know the object in the first way, as eye-sensitivity. You may start with knowing consciousness, with contact, or with feeling.

M04-body-P102.title: Apprehending individual mental phenomena in the mind-door process

paragraphs.M04-body-P102-S01: If you begin from knowing consciousness, practise seeing repeatedly with wisdom that knowing consciousness arises once at mind-door adverting, seven times at impulsion and twice at registration. When eye-sensitivity appears at the clear life-continuum, the mind-door, use that door and the heart-base to practise seeing mind-door processes recur with many life-continuum moments between them.
paragraphs.M04-body-P102-S02: When successful, add one mental factor at a time: knowing consciousness and contact in pairs, then add feeling for groups of three, perception for groups of four, and so on. Practise until you see the complete set arising together in each moment: twelve at mind-door adverting, thirty-four at each impulsion, and thirty-four at each registration. If mentality becomes indistinct, re-establish a fourth-jhāna concentration. Once the light of wisdom is strong again, apprehend both the object being discerned, such as eye-sensitivity, and the clear life-continuum, and add one mental phenomenon at a time. Practise repeatedly, apprehending the mind-door and the object together. Use this method whenever the mental phenomena are unclear.
paragraphs.M04-body-P102-S03: When able to see with wisdom, see these phenomena incline towards eye-sensitivity as object and apprehend them as “mentality, mentality”. Discern in the same way in the remaining kinds of wise attention. When discerning in this way, at impulsion and registration…

M04-body-P103.title: Four cases of association with knowledge and joy

paragraphs.M04-body-P103-S01:
1. Sometimes both knowledge and joy are present. This is great wholesome consciousness accompanied by joyful feeling and associated with knowledge.
2. Sometimes knowledge is present without joy. This is great wholesome consciousness accompanied by equanimous feeling and associated with knowledge.
3. Sometimes joy is present without knowledge. This is great wholesome consciousness accompanied by joyful feeling and dissociated from knowledge.
4. Sometimes neither knowledge nor joy is present. This is great wholesome consciousness accompanied by equanimous feeling and dissociated from knowledge.
There are four cases in all.
paragraphs.M04-body-P103-S02: When discerning eye-sensitivity as eye-sensitivity, there are four modes according to whether knowledge and joy are present. Likewise discern four modes each when knowing eye-sensitivity as materiality, impermanent, suffering, non-self and unattractive. In all there are twenty-four instances.
paragraphs.M04-body-P103-S03: There are four prompted (sasaṅkhārika) and four unprompted (asaṅkhārika) types of great wholesome consciousness, eight in all. Prompted means with inducement, unprompted without inducement. Since this distinction does not change the number of mental factors, only the four modes above are presented here. As meditators discern, they gradually understand the nature of the prompted and unprompted types. The four modes in each group together make eight types of great wholesome consciousness. The same applies to great functional consciousness, which arises only in the continuum of arahants.

paragraphs.M04-body-P104-S01: Generally, registration can occur only when impulsion is sense-sphere, the being is a sense-sphere being, and the object is sense-sphere, very great at the five doors or clear at the mind-door. Sense-sphere objects comprise sense-sphere consciousness and mental factors and the twenty-eight material phenomena. In a sense-sphere being’s continuum, registration may follow sense-sphere impulsions in mind-door processes taking sense-sphere consciousness and mental factors as object. As the twenty-eight material phenomena are also sense-sphere phenomena, registration may follow sense-sphere impulsions in processes taking them as object. But in five-door processes such as the eye-door process the object must be very great, and in mind-door processes it must be clear. Hence “generally”. Under this condition registration cannot follow impulsions in a process that takes a concept as object.
paragraphs.M04-body-P104-S02: The Sammohavinodanī commentary on the Vibhaṅga explains as follows.
paragraphs.M04-body-P104-S03:
Tilakkhaṇārammaṇikavipassanāya tadārammaṇaṃ na labbhati.
Registration does not occur after insight impulsion taking one of the three characteristics as object (Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 2, p. 147).
paragraphs.M04-body-P104-S04: The teachers explain that this statement about registration being unable to follow insight impulsion refers specifically to strong insight impulsion. They cite the following canonical and commentarial passages.

paragraphs.M04-body-P105-S01:
Sekkhā vā puthujjanā vā kusalaṃ aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassanti. Kusale niruddhe vipāko tadārammaṇatā uppajjati.
Paṭṭhāna, vol. 1, p. 133.
paragraphs.M04-body-P105-S02:
Kusale niruddheti vipassanāvasena pavattitvā niruddhe. Vipākoti kāmāvacaravipāko. Tadārammaṇatāti tadārammaṇatāya. Taṃ kusalassa javanassa ārammaṇabhūtaṃ vipassitakusalaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā uppajjatīti attho.
Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 3, p. 436.
paragraphs.M04-body-P105-S03: Trainees and worldlings discern wholesome mentality by one of the three characteristics, impermanence, suffering or non-self. After that wholesome insight impulsion, sense-sphere resultant mentality takes the same wholesome mentality that was discerned, the very object taken by the impulsion. It arises to perform the function of registration (Paṭṭhāna, vol. 1, p. 133. Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 3, p. 436).
paragraphs.M04-body-P105-S04: Here the object of insight knowledge is wholesome, and the series of insight impulsions discerning it is wholesome as well. Because the object is sense-sphere wholesome, the insight impulsion discerning it is great wholesome sense-sphere impulsion. All three factors are present: sense-sphere impulsion, a sense-sphere being, and a sense-sphere object. Since the teaching says registration can follow this insight impulsion, the teachers explain that the passage refers to insight impulsion that is still weak (see Mūlaṭīkā, vol. 1, p. 131).

M04-body-P106.title: Conditions and kinds of registration consciousness

paragraphs.M04-body-P106-S01: At this stage the meditator is still at the knowledge that delimits mentality and materiality, apprehending mentality that arises with sense-sphere materiality as object. The actual insight stage has yet to be reached. Here, when apprehending mentality taking materiality as object, registration may also follow the great wholesome impulsions of the knowledge that apprehends materiality if that material object is clear.
paragraphs.M04-body-P106-S02: After great wholesome impulsions, great resultant consciousness performing registration may be accompanied by joyful or equanimous feeling as appropriate. Rootless investigating consciousness may also perform registration as appropriate. After unwholesome impulsions, great resultant and rootless investigating consciousness may also perform that function as appropriate. The preceding table illustrates only great resultant registration under the general rule. Meditators can gradually understand the other cases as they discern. Under the general rule, joyful registration follows joyful impulsions, and equanimous registration follows equanimous or displeased impulsions.
paragraphs.M04-body-P106-S03: The eight great resultant and three investigating consciousnesses, eleven in all, are called registration because they can perform the function of continuing to receive the very object taken by impulsion. The following table shows registration that can follow impulsion, especially for good meditators who are three-rooted worldlings. Stream-enterers, once-returners and non-returners can understand it similarly, leaving out the defilements they have abandoned.

M04-body-P107.title: Registration table and the distinction between resultants and impulsion

paragraphs.M04-body-P107-S01:
Registration for three-rooted worldlings
After impulsion | Possible registration
Any of the 8 great wholesome impulsions | Any of the 11 registration consciousnesses
Any of the 8 greed-rooted impulsions | Any of the 11 registration consciousnesses
Either of the 2 hatred-rooted impulsions | Any of the 6 equanimous registration consciousnesses
Either of the 2 delusion-rooted impulsions | Any of the 11 registration consciousnesses
paragraphs.M04-body-P107-S02: 1. Naturally desirable or exceptionally desirable objects are encountered owing to previous wholesome kamma. With a moderately desirable object, the process consciousnesses apart from adverting and impulsion are great resultant or rootless wholesome resultant consciousnesses. At the five doors these are five-door sense consciousness, receiving, investigating and registration. At the mind-door this refers to registration. With wise attention wholesome impulsion can occur. With unwise attention unwholesome impulsion can occur.
paragraphs.M04-body-P107-S03: 2. With an exceptionally desirable and precious object such as the Buddha, only the five joyful types of wholesome-resultant registration can occur. Impulsion may be wholesome with wise attention or unwholesome with unwise attention.
paragraphs.M04-body-P107-S04: 3. Naturally undesirable objects are encountered owing to previous unwholesome kamma. With such an object, wise attention leads to wholesome impulsion and unwise attention to unwholesome impulsion. In five-door processes, the five kinds of sense consciousness such as eye-consciousness…

paragraphs.M04-body-P108-S01: … together with receiving, investigating and registration, and the registration in mind-door processes, must be rootless unwholesome-resultant consciousnesses. Under this rule, with an undesirable object there is only one kind of registration, namely unwholesome-resultant investigating consciousness accompanied by equanimity.
paragraphs.M04-body-P108-S02: The tables illustrate the general rule. Under it joyful registration follows joyful impulsion, and equanimous registration follows equanimous or displeased impulsion. For a being reborn with joyful consciousness, the life-continuum is of the same type as rebirth-linking and is also joyful. If hatred-rooted impulsion arises in that being’s continuum and for some reason registration cannot follow, ordinarily life-continuum would follow the hatred-rooted impulsion. But rebirth-linking, life-continuum and death consciousness in one life are of the same type, so here the life-continuum must be joyful. Joyful life-continuum cannot suitably follow hatred-rooted impulsion immediately. In this difficulty one of the two kinds of equanimous investigating consciousness arises as guest life-continuum, linking the hatred-rooted impulsion with the original joyful life-continuum. It is unwholesome resultant if the object is undesirable and wholesome resultant if the object is desirable or exceptionally desirable.
paragraphs.M04-body-P108-S03: Guest life-continuum (āgantukabhavaṅga). The life-continuum moments that begin to occur after rebirth-linking are of the same type as rebirth-linking. Being present from the beginning in the house of the aggregates and residing there, they are called resident life-continuum (āvāsikabhavaṅga)…

M04-body-P109.title: The object of guest life-continuum and three cases without registration

paragraphs.M04-body-P109-S01: … the householder life-continuum. Equanimous investigating consciousness arises only occasionally when a difficulty like the one above occurs, so it is called guest life-continuum. Since it does not take the object taken by impulsion, it is not called registration. Nor can it take the resident life-continuum’s object. It takes a previously familiar sense-sphere object. If that familiar object, to which much attention has been given, is desirable, the investigating consciousness accompanied by equanimity is wholesome resultant. If it is undesirable, the investigating consciousness accompanied by equanimity is unwholesome resultant.
paragraphs.M04-body-P109-S02: 1. A person with joyful rebirth-linking who holds wrong view may have hatred-rooted impulsion with an exceptionally desirable object such as the Buddha as a very great or clear object. Or a person with joyful rebirth-linking may have hatred-rooted impulsion from fright at a celestial maiden, an exceptionally desirable object that is very great or clear. There is no opportunity for registration after that hatred-rooted impulsion. With an exceptionally desirable object only joyful registration is possible, and joyful registration cannot suitably follow hatred-rooted impulsion.
paragraphs.M04-body-P109-S03: 2. If a person with joyful rebirth-linking has hatred-rooted impulsion taking a sense-sphere object that is large or indistinct, registration does not follow it. Registration has an opportunity only with a very great object at the five doors or a clear object at the mind-door.
paragraphs.M04-body-P109-S04: 3. If a meditator with joyful rebirth-linking attains jhāna and then loses it, they may take the lost exalted jhāna as object and have hatred-rooted impulsion: “My sublime attainment has been lost!” As the object is exalted, registration does not occur.

M04-body-P110.title: The linking function of guest life-continuum

paragraphs.M04-body-P110-S01: 4. If a person with joyful rebirth-linking has hatred-rooted impulsion taking a concept as object, registration does not occur with that concept, because it is not a sense-sphere object.
paragraphs.M04-body-P110-S02: In such processes, where registration has no opportunity to arise, the original joyful life-continuum, of the same type as rebirth-linking, also cannot follow hatred-rooted impulsion immediately. Because neither registration nor the original life-continuum can immediately follow, investigating consciousness accompanied by equanimity arises as guest life-continuum, linking hatred-rooted impulsion to the original joyful life-continuum.
paragraphs.M04-body-P110-S03: To understand one case of registration according to the explanations above, the table of wholesome bare mind-door processes taking mind objects is presented again below. Use it to understand the remaining tables similarly. Remember the general rule: joyful registration follows joyful impulsion and equanimous registration follows equanimous impulsion, as appropriate. With an undesirable object, however, the resultant five-door sense consciousness, receiving, investigating and registration in five-door processes must be unwholesome resultants. Thus even when joyful impulsion occurs with an undesirable object, registration can only be unwholesome-resultant investigating consciousness with equanimity, comprising eleven mental phenomena. Wholesome-resultant investigating consciousness with equanimity also has eleven mental phenomena (see the visible-object process table). Thus when the table shows eleven, understand this as unwholesome-resultant equanimous investigating for an undesirable object and wholesome-resultant equanimous investigating for a desirable object.

M04-body-P111.title: Wholesome mind-door process table with concrete materiality as object

M04-body-P112.title: Registration with undesirable and desirable objects

paragraphs.M04-body-P112-S01: The table shows joyful registration following joyful impulsion and equanimous registration following equanimous impulsion. With wise attention, even when encountering an undesirable object, joyful or equanimous impulsion can arise as appropriate. Because the object is undesirable, however, only the rootless unwholesome-resultant investigating consciousness accompanied by equanimity can occur as registration.
paragraphs.M04-body-P112-S02: With a moderately desirable object, wise attention may lead to joyful or equanimous impulsion as appropriate. Either rooted great-resultant registration or rootless wholesome-resultant registration may occur. In a single process only one of these kinds occurs. If great wholesome impulsion is joyful and associated with knowledge, registration may be joyful great resultant associated with knowledge or joyful rootless wholesome-resultant investigating consciousness. If great wholesome impulsion is equanimous and associated with knowledge, registration may be equanimous great resultant associated with knowledge or equanimous rootless wholesome-resultant investigating consciousness. Understand the joyful and equanimous cases dissociated from knowledge similarly, with knowledge absent.
paragraphs.M04-body-P112-S03: If the object is exceptionally desirable, wise attention can lead to joyful or equanimous impulsion as appropriate. Joyful feeling, however, is more frequent.

M04-body-P113.title: Reading the registration counts and discerning concrete materiality

paragraphs.M04-body-P113-S01: One of five kinds can occur as registration, as appropriate: four joyful great-resultant registration consciousnesses and one joyful rootless wholesome-resultant investigating consciousness.
paragraphs.M04-body-P113-S02: Accordingly the rootless registration column gives 12/11 or 11/11. The first number 12 refers to the group of mental phenomena in joyful rootless wholesome-resultant registration. The first number 11 refers to equanimous rootless wholesome-resultant investigating registration. The second number 11 refers to equanimous rootless unwholesome-resultant investigating registration when the object is undesirable.
paragraphs.M04-body-P113-S03: Concrete material phenomena to discern following the example: 1. Ear-sensitivity. 2. Nose-sensitivity. 3. Tongue-sensitivity. 4. Body-sensitivity. 5. Water element. 6. Femininity materiality. 7. Masculinity materiality. 8. Heart-base. 9. Material life faculty. 10. Nutriment.
paragraphs.M04-body-P113-S04: Including eye-sensitivity, eleven concrete material phenomena belong to the mind-object group. Analyse the material cluster containing the material phenomenon you wish to take as object, select that concrete material phenomenon as object, and seek and apprehend the mentality arising with it as object. When discerning internally, male meditators take masculinity materiality and female meditators femininity materiality, and apprehend the mentality arising with the respective object…

paragraphs.M04-body-P114-S01: … alone. The method of practice is the same for the two sex materialities. Taken collectively, one may seek and apprehend mentality arising with both kinds of sex materiality as objects.
paragraphs.M04-body-P114-S02: The ten non-concrete material phenomena, those without individual nature in the mind-object group, are not material phenomena to be discerned in insight by the three characteristics. Thus whether one discerns one or all of them as impermanent, processes with insight impulsion knowing “impermanent” cannot arise. Understand suffering and non-self similarly. For each non-concrete material phenomenon, therefore, discern in only two ways, for example:
paragraphs.M04-body-P114-S03:
1. Discern it as the space element. Discern four cases of consciousness and mental factors knowing it as the space element, varying the presence of knowledge and joy.
2. Discern that same space element as materiality. Discern four cases of consciousness and mental factors knowing it as materiality, varying the presence of knowledge and joy.
paragraphs.M04-body-P114-S04: Here too, first see the space element as the gaps between material clusters. Then apprehend the mentality taking that space element as object. Understand the same pattern for all the non-concrete material phenomena below.

Ageing (jaratā). 9. Impermanence (aniccatā).

M04-body-P116.title: Analysing material clusters before apprehending mentality

paragraphs.M04-body-P116-S01: To seek and apprehend mentality taking non-concrete materiality as object, analyse the cluster containing the materiality to be discerned until wisdom sees the ultimate materiality originated by consciousness, temperature, or nutriment in the same cluster. Then select the particular materiality to be discerned. Material phenomena arise in clusters or groups.
paragraphs.M04-body-P116-S02: First see the material cluster. Analyse it by wisdom into the individual ultimate material phenomena, all eight, nine, or ten according to the cluster. Then select a concrete material phenomenon such as eye-sensitivity, or a non-concrete one such as bodily intimation. When it appears before the clear life-continuum, the mind-door, seek and apprehend the mentality arising with it as object.
paragraphs.M04-body-P116-S03: The foregoing explained how to apprehend mentality in mind-door processes with wholesome impulsion that take concrete or non-concrete materiality belonging to the mind-object domain as object. For convenience, the impulsion mentality and great-resultant registration mentality are called the faith-and-wisdom group. Next comes apprehending mentality in wholesome mind-door processes associated with abstinence and immeasurable mental factors.

paragraphs.M04-body-P117-S01: Of the three abstinence factors (virati), right speech is abstaining from four kinds of verbal misconduct apart from livelihood. Discern the four cases separately because their objects differ: take abstaining from lying as object once, abstaining from divisive speech once, abstaining from harsh speech once, and abstaining from idle chatter once. For each, discern four cases according to the presence or absence of knowledge and joy.
paragraphs.M04-body-P117-S02:
1. Apprehend the clear life-continuum, the mind-door, at the earlier time when you abstained from lying.
2. Direct the mind to that past abstention from lying.
3. When that object appears at the mind-door, apprehend the mind-door impulsion mentality that arose at the time of abstaining.
paragraphs.M04-body-P117-S03: In each impulsion, adding right speech to the thirty-four mental phenomena of the faith-and-wisdom group makes thirty-five. Discern four cases varying knowledge and joy. With a clear object, rooted great-resultant or rootless registration may occur as appropriate. If registration is great resultant, right speech…

paragraphs.M04-body-P118-S01: … cannot be associated with it. Only mental phenomena of the faith-and-wisdom group occur, with thirty-four as appropriate. Discern four cases varying knowledge and joy. Discern abstention from divisive speech, harsh speech and idle chatter in the same way.
paragraphs.M04-body-P118-S02: Right action is abstaining from three kinds of bodily misconduct apart from livelihood. Discern three cases separately because their objects differ: take abstaining from killing as object once, abstaining from taking what is not given once, and abstaining from sexual misconduct once. In each case discern four modes varying knowledge and joy.
paragraphs.M04-body-P118-S03:
1. Apprehend the clear life-continuum, the mind-door, at the time of abstaining from killing.
2. Direct the mind to that past abstention. For example, attend to an occasion when you refrained from killing a mosquito.
3. When the object appears at the mind-door, apprehend the mentality in the mind-door process with great wholesome impulsion that arose at the time of abstaining.
paragraphs.M04-body-P118-S04: In each impulsion, adding right action to the thirty-four mental phenomena of the faith-and-wisdom group makes thirty-five. Varying the presence of knowledge and joy, discern four…

paragraphs.M04-body-P119-S01: … cases. If the object is clear, registration can occur, either rooted great-resultant or rootless registration as appropriate. Right action cannot be associated with great-resultant registration. There can be thirty-four mental phenomena of the faith-and-wisdom group in great-resultant registration as appropriate. Discern four cases varying knowledge and joy. Discern abstention from taking what is not given and from sexual misconduct similarly.
paragraphs.M04-body-P119-S02: Right livelihood is abstaining from bodily and verbal misconduct connected with livelihood. With three kinds of bodily and four kinds of verbal misconduct, there are various ways of discerning. Take one object in relation to which you habitually abstain or have abstained. For example, refrain from eating a food when you know an animal was killed specifically for you.
paragraphs.M04-body-P119-S03:
1. Apprehend the clear life-continuum, the mind-door, at the time when you abstained from wrong livelihood.
2. Direct the mind to one occasion of abstaining from wrong livelihood. For example, if you refrained from eating unsuitable meat or fish, attend to that abstention.
3. When the object appears at the mind-door, apprehend the mentality in the mind-door process with great wholesome impulsion that arose at the time of abstaining. Registration may occur.

M04-body-P121.title: Three senses of right speech and right action

paragraphs.M04-body-P121-S01: Right speech is of three kinds: right speech as the utterance (kathāsammāvācā), as volition (cetanāsammāvācā), and as abstinence (viratisammāvācā). Good, faultless speech connected with causes and effects is right speech as utterance. The volition associated with preparatory, direct-knowledge, great wholesome or great functional impulsion that brings about such faultless speech is right speech as volition. When there is an occasion for lying, divisive speech, harsh speech or idle chatter, one may abstain and instead speak truthfully, harmoniously, gently or beneficially, or one may remain silent. The abstinence present in the consciousness that arises in speaking or remaining silent is right speech as abstinence. The misconduct abstained from through right speech here is apart from livelihood.
paragraphs.M04-body-P121-S02: Right action likewise has three kinds: right action as activity, as volition, and as abstinence. The bodily activity of someone doing a faultless deed, such as giving, keeping precepts or developing meditation, is right action as activity. The volition that performs that faultless deed is right action as volition. When an opportunity for bodily misconduct arises and one refrains, whether or not one performs some other bodily action, this is right action as abstinence. All misconduct abstained from in this sense is apart from livelihood.

M04-body-P122.title: Right livelihood and two kinds of mundane abstinence

paragraphs.M04-body-P122-S01: Right livelihood has two kinds: right livelihood as activity and right livelihood as abstinence. Rightful activity in making a living by an ordinary occupation such as farming or trade, or in a renunciant’s seeking the four requisites in accordance with the Dhamma while avoiding wrong livelihood such as cultivating donor families and procuring requisites through gifts, is right livelihood as activity. Refraining from bodily and verbal misconduct connected with livelihood, or from using the four requisites obtained through such wrong livelihood, is right livelihood as abstinence.
paragraphs.M04-body-P122-S02: There are three kinds of abstinence: abstinence upon encountering an occasion (sampattavirati), abstinence through undertaking precepts (samādānavirati), and abstinence through eradication (samucchedavirati). Someone who has not undertaken the training rules reflects on family, age, learning or good fortune and thinks, “It is unfitting for us to do such a wrong deed.” Encountering an object in relation to which a transgression is possible, that person refrains. The abstinence arising in that continuum is abstinence upon encountering an occasion (Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 1, p. 146).
paragraphs.M04-body-P122-S03: Someone who undertakes the training rules, whether at the time of undertaking them or later, refrains from transgression because of the undertaking, even at the cost of their life. The abstinence arising in that continuum is abstinence through undertaking precepts (Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 1, p. 146).

M04-body-P123.title: Abstinence through eradication and objects of mundane abstinence

paragraphs.M04-body-P123-S01: Abstinence through eradication is abstinence associated with the noble path. It arises through cutting off at the root the latent tendencies underlying unwholesome conduct and wrong livelihood. From its arising onward, even the thought “I will kill a living being” does not arise in a noble disciple’s continuum (Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 1, p. 147). Being associated with the noble path, it clearly takes Nibbāna as object. The objects of abstinence upon encountering an occasion and abstinence through undertaking call for further examination.
paragraphs.M04-body-P123-S02:
Ārammaṇato pāṇātipāto jīvitindriyārammaṇo. Adinnādānaṃ sattārammaṇaṃ vā saṅkhārārammaṇaṃ vā. Micchācāro itthipurisārammaṇo. Musāvādo sattārammaṇo vā saṅkhārārammaṇo vā. Surāpānaṃ saṅkhārārammaṇaṃ.
Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 2, p. 366.
paragraphs.M04-body-P123-S03:
Satta-itthi-purisārammaṇato tathāgahitasaṅkhārārammaṇatāya dhammā.
Mūlaṭīkā, vol. 2, p. 189.
paragraphs.M04-body-P123-S04: As to objects, killing takes the life faculty as object. Taking what is not given and similar cases can take a being or formations as object. Sexual misconduct takes a woman or a man as object. False speech can take a being or formations as object. Taking intoxicants has formations as object (Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 2, p. 366). According to the Mūlaṭīkā, phenomena described as taking a being, woman or man as object have the corresponding formations as object (vol. 2, p. 189).
paragraphs.M04-body-P123-S05:
Ārammaṇato pāṇātipātā veramaṇī parassa jīvitindriyaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā attano veracetanāya viramati. Itarāsupi eseva nayo. Sabbāpi hi etā vītikkamitabbavatthuṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā veracetanāhiyeva viramanti.
Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 2, p. 368.
paragraphs.M04-body-P123-S06: When abstaining from killing, one takes the life faculty of the being that could be killed as object and refrains from the volition to transgress. Similar cases follow the same principle, because abstinence arises by taking the object in relation to which transgression is possible and refraining from the volition to transgress (Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 2, p. 368).
paragraphs.M04-body-P123-S07:
Parittārammaṇā… pe… paccuppannārammaṇā… pe… bahiddhārammaṇā.
Taking a limited object… pe… taking a present object… pe… taking an external object (Abhidhamma, vol. 2, p. 205).

M04-body-P124.title: The object in relation to which one could transgress, and the volition to transgress

paragraphs.M04-body-P124-S01:
Ārammaṇattikesu pana yāni sikkhāpadāni ettha sattārammaṇānīti vuttāni, tāni yasmā sattoti saṅkhaṃ gate saṅkhāreyeva ārammaṇaṃ karonti, yasmā ca sabbānipi etāni sampattavirativaseneva niddiṭṭhāni, tasmā “parittārammaṇā”ti ca “paccuppannārammaṇā”ti ca vuttā. Yato pana viramati, tassa vatthuno accantabahiddhattā sabbesampi bahiddhārammaṇatā veditabbāti.
Among the object triads, the training rules described here as taking a being as object take as object the very formations designated “a being”. Since all these rules are explained in terms of abstinence upon encountering an occasion, they are said to take a limited object and a present object. Since the basis in relation to which one abstains is entirely external, all are to be understood as taking an external object. (Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 2, p. 369.)
paragraphs.M04-body-P124-S02: “Volition of abstinence upon encountering an occasion” means volition with a present object on that occasion, in relation to which one abstains from transgression (Mūlaṭīkā, vol. 2, p. 190).
paragraphs.M04-body-P124-S03:
Sampattaviraticetanāti sampatte paccuppanne ārammaṇe yathāviramitabbato viraticetanāti attho.
Mūlaṭīkā, vol. 2, p. 190.
paragraphs.M04-body-P124-S04: The meaning of the canonical, commentarial and subcommentarial passages above is as follows. Abstinence upon encountering an occasion and abstinence through undertaking take as object only limited sense-sphere phenomena, called the basis in relation to which one could transgress (vītikkamitabbavatthu) or should abstain (viramitabbavatthu). These are formations of sense-sphere mentality and materiality. The object is present and is external mentality and materiality.
paragraphs.M04-body-P124-S05: The unwholesome volition to transgress in relation to that object is the volition of transgression (veracetanā), the real enemy. When the sense-sphere mentality and materiality in relation to which one could transgress are taken as object, the nature of refraining from the volition of transgression in one’s own continuum is abstinence. Abstinence from killing takes another being’s life faculty as object and refrains from the unwholesome volition to transgress in one’s own continuum. Abstinence from taking what is not given takes that in relation to which one could transgress…

M04-body-P125.title: Objects of particular kinds of abstinence

paragraphs.M04-body-P125-S01: … either a being or formations as object, and refrains from the volition to transgress that has arisen in one’s own continuum. Abstinence from sexual misconduct takes a woman or a man, the possible object of transgression, as object, and refrains from the volition of sexual misconduct in one’s own continuum. Abstinence from lying takes a being or formations, the possible object of transgression, as object, and refrains from the volition to lie in one’s own continuum. Abstinence from intoxicants takes formations constituting an intoxicant, the possible object of transgression, as object, and refrains from the unwholesome volition to take it in one’s own continuum (Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 2, pp. 366–368).
paragraphs.M04-body-P125-S02: The explanation that abstinence takes a being, woman or man as object means that it takes only the formations, sense-sphere mentality and materiality, which exist in a manner that can be designated a being, woman or man (Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 2, p. 369. Mūlaṭīkā, vol. 2, p. 187).
paragraphs.M04-body-P125-S03: Only on encountering a present object in relation to which a transgression is possible does abstinence take that object and refrain from the unwholesome volition to transgress arising in one’s continuum. Thus abstinence upon encountering an occasion and abstinence through undertaking take present sense-sphere mentality and materiality in relation to which transgression is possible as object. That mentality and materiality are external.

paragraphs.M04-body-P126-S01: It remains to examine whether abstinence takes a being, woman, or man as object. If it takes such objects, there is no opportunity for registration.
paragraphs.M04-body-P126-S02: Compassion (karuṇā) is wishing to rescue a suffering being. 1. Apprehend the clear life-continuum, the mind-door. 2. Direct the mind to a suffering being you wish to rescue. 3. When that conceptual object of a being appears at the mind-door, apprehend the series of mind-door processes with impulsion in which compassion predominates. The thirty-four mental phenomena of the faith-and-wisdom group plus compassion make thirty-five as appropriate. Discern the four cases varying knowledge and joy.
paragraphs.M04-body-P126-S03: Appreciative joy (muditā) is rejoicing in the happiness of a being. 1. Apprehend the clear life-continuum, the mind-door. 2. Direct the mind to a happy being. 3. When that conceptual object of a happy being appears at the mind-door, apprehend the series of mind-door processes with impulsion that arose.

M04-body-P127.title: Feeling in appreciative joy, faith and wisdom

paragraphs.M04-body-P127-S01: If appreciative joy has not matured to the attainment of its jhāna, its impulsion should have joyful feeling only. Discern the two cases, with and without knowledge. With knowledge, thirty-four plus appreciative joy makes thirty-five. Without knowledge, thirty-three plus appreciative joy makes thirty-four. Venerable Anuruddha holds that for one who has developed appreciative joy to jhāna, the strength of development also allows access impulsions accompanied by equanimity. Such a person can discern four cases varying knowledge and joy. Since compassion and appreciative joy take a being as a concept, registration cannot follow their impulsions. For apprehending their jhāna mentality, see the tables on the divine abidings.
paragraphs.M04-body-P127-S02: In the groups of impulsion mentality containing abstinence or immeasurable factors, faith is confidence in kamma and its results. Wisdom is understanding kamma and its results, right view of ownership of kamma (kammassakatā sammādiṭṭhi). Alternatively, faith in abstinence is confidence in training in virtue. Here the special reference is to the sense-sphere impulsions called preparation and access that precede jhāna with compassion or appreciative joy.

M04-body-P128.title: Table of immeasurable factors and recollection of the Buddha

paragraphs.M04-body-P128-S01:

Immeasurable factor | Mind-door adverting | Impulsion (7 times)

2. Appreciative joy | 12 | 35

paragraphs.M04-body-P128-S02: If you have developed the four protective meditation subjects, apprehend the series of mind-door processes with great wholesome impulsion taking the Buddha’s qualities as object. The impulsion mentality belongs to the faith-and-wisdom group. Recollection of the Buddha reaches access concentration only, so there are just seven impulsion moments. Registration may or may not follow. The Buddha’s qualities…

M04-body-P129.title: The Buddha’s qualities as mind-door objects

paragraphs.M04-body-P129-S01: … include both mundane and supramundane qualities. For example, the Buddha’s generosity, virtue, concentration up to access, insight knowledge, teaching knowledge and omniscience, in terms of actual phenomena, are series of unprompted, knowledge-associated great functional impulsions of the sense sphere. If recollection takes such qualities as object, registration has an opportunity to follow the meditator’s great wholesome impulsion because the object is sense-sphere. With a clear object registration may occur, and with an indistinct one it does not. It is very difficult, however, to penetrate the Buddha’s qualities to the level of ultimate reality.
paragraphs.M04-body-P129-S02: The Buddha’s absorption concentration and direct knowledges are exalted functional phenomena. His path and fruition knowledges are supramundane wisdom. When recollection takes these exalted or supramundane qualities of concentration and wisdom as object, registration cannot follow the meditator’s great wholesome impulsion because the object is outside the sense sphere.
paragraphs.M04-body-P129-S03: If registration occurs, it may be rooted or rootless as appropriate. However, “atikuddake pana somanassasahagatāneva santīraṇatadārammaṇāni”: with an exceptionally desirable object, investigating and registration are accompanied only by joy. The Buddha’s qualities are exceptionally desirable, so only one of the five joyful registrations can occur as appropriate.

paragraphs.M04-body-P130-S01: Recollection of death also reaches access concentration only. Its meditation impulsions are sense-sphere access impulsions and occur seven times. Registration may or may not follow. If one takes the cutting off of one’s life faculty as object, that life faculty consists of material life and the mental life associated with death consciousness, so the object is sense-sphere. If it is clear, there is opportunity for registration. If indistinct, there is none.
paragraphs.M04-body-P130-S02: If one cannot take the cutting off of the life faculty as object and remains only with the concept “I am dying”, registration cannot follow those impulsions of recollection of death. Only one who has apprehended mentality and materiality at the level of ultimate reality can take the cutting off of material and mental life at that level. For one who has yet to attain such knowledge of delimiting mentality and materiality, the mind in recollection of death will generally remain with the concept “I am dying”.

M04-body-P131.title: Mind-door process table for recollection of the Buddha and death

paragraphs.M04-body-P131-S02: Note: In recollection of the Buddha it is very difficult for joyful registration to arise after equanimous impulsion. Since the object is exceptionally desirable, equanimous registration also has no opportunity to follow equanimous impulsion. Apprehend the phenomena in practice to know for certain.
paragraphs.M04-body-P131-S03: A person who has developed recollection of the Buddha and wishes to apprehend mentality taking his qualities as object should: 1. Apprehend the clear life-continuum, the mind-door. 2. Direct the mind to a quality of the Buddha you favour. 3. When that quality appears at the mind-door, apprehend the mentality in the resulting series of mind-door processes with impulsion.

M04-body-P132.title: From recollection of death to five-door processes

paragraphs.M04-body-P132-S01: A meditator who has developed recollection of death and wishes to apprehend mentality taking the severing of their life faculty as object should: 1. Apprehend the clear life-continuum, the mind-door. 2. Direct the mind to the severing of your life faculty. 3. When that object appears at the mind-door, apprehend the mentality in the resulting series of mind-door processes with impulsion. When apprehending mentality taking a Buddha quality or death as object, you may extend the discernment according to your wisdom.
paragraphs.M04-body-P132-S02: The foregoing presented the method for apprehending mind-door process series with great wholesome impulsion in the domain of mind objects. Next comes the method for apprehending mentality in five-door processes with great wholesome impulsion.
paragraphs.M04-body-P132-S03:
Tattha ekekaṃ ārammaṇaṃ dvisu dvisu dvāresu āpāthamāgacchati. Rūpārammaṇañhi cakkhupasādaṃ ghaṭṭetvā taṅkhaṇaññeva manodvāre āpāthamāgacchati, bhavaṅgacalanassa paccayo hotīti attho. Sadda-gandha-rasa-phoṭṭhabbārammaṇesupi eseva nayo. Yathā hi sakuṇo ākāsenāgantvā rukkhagge nilīyamānova rukkhasākhaṃ ghaṭṭeti, chāyā cassa pathaviyaṃ paṭihaññati, sākhāghaṭṭana-chāyāpharaṇāni apubbaṃ acarimaṃ ekakkhaṇeyeva bhavanti. Evaṃ paccuppannarūpādīnaṃ cakkhupasādādighaṭṭanānañca bhavaṅga-
Quotation continued on Burmese page 133.
paragraphs.M04-body-P132-S04: Points to know beforehand. One object comes into range at two doors. A visible object impinges on eye-sensitivity and at the same time enters the range of the mind-door, meaning that it causes the life-continuum to vibrate. Sounds, odours, tastes and tangibles follow the same pattern. As a bird descending from the sky alights on a branch and its shadow simultaneously appears on the ground, its touch and shadow occur together…

M04-body-P133.title: One object appears simultaneously at two doors

paragraphs.M04-body-P133-S01:
calanasamatthatāya manodvāre āpāthagamanāñca apubbaṃ acarimaṃ ekakkhaṇeyeva hoti. Tato bhavaṅgaṃ vicchinditvā cakkhudvārādīsu uppannānaṃ āvajjanādīnaṃ voṭṭhabbanapariyosānānaṃ anantarā tesaṃ ārammaṇānaṃ aññatarasmiṃ idaṃ mahācittaṃ uppajjati.
Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 1, p. 114.
paragraphs.M04-body-P133-S02:
… so too, when a visible object impinges on eye-sensitivity and can cause the life-continuum to vibrate, impingement and coming into mind-door range occur simultaneously. After the life-continuum stops, following adverting and other consciousnesses and their associated phenomena, a great wholesome consciousness arises taking one of those objects (Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 1, p. 114).
Āpāthamāgacchati manasā pañcaviññāṇehi ca gahetabbabhāvūpagamanena. Ghaṭṭetvā paṭimukhabhāvāpāthaṃ gantvā.
“Comes into range” means becoming accessible to the mind and the five sense consciousnesses. “Impinges” means coming into range directly before the corresponding door. (Mūlaṭīkā, vol. 1, p. 70.)
paragraphs.M04-body-P133-S03: 1. A visible object appears at the eye-door and mind-door. 2. A sound appears at the ear-door and mind-door. 3. An odour appears at the nose-door and mind-door. 4. A taste appears at the tongue-door and mind-door. 5. A tangible object appears at the body-door and mind-door. Thus each object appears simultaneously at two doors. When the object appears, sense consciousness such as eye-consciousness and mind consciousness such as five-door adverting arise in the fixed order of the process. The object must therefore appear at the corresponding sense door for sense consciousness to know it, and at the life-continuum, the mind-door, for mind consciousness to know it.
paragraphs.M04-body-P133-S04: When a visible object impinges on eye-sensitivity, it appears at that very time at the life-continuum, the mind-door, and makes it vibrate. Understand the same for sound, odour, taste…

M04-body-P134.title: The simile of the alighting bird and its shadow

paragraphs.M04-body-P134-S01: … and tangible objects (Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 1, p. 114). The commentary uses “ghaṭṭetvā”, meaning touching or striking. One might think a visible object actually strikes both the eye-door and mind-door. This refers to the object and door coming close enough to have the effect of impingement (Mūlaṭīkā, vol. 1, p. 70).
paragraphs.M04-body-P134-S02: For example, a bird flying down lands on a branch. As the bird touches the branch, its shadow touches the ground. The two occur simultaneously, neither before nor after the other. Likewise, a present visible object impinges on eye-sensitivity and comes before the mind-door by its ability to make the life-continuum vibrate. The two occur simultaneously, neither before nor after. After the life-continuum vibrates and ceases, following the process consciousnesses from adverting through determining at the eye-door or the other sense doors, the first great wholesome consciousness arises to perform impulsion regarding one of the objects such as visible form, according to how it is attended to (Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 1, p. 114).

M04-body-P135.title: Eye-door process abbreviations and past life-continuum

paragraphs.M04-body-P135-S01: The eye-door process abbreviations denote past life-continuum (atītabhavaṅga), vibration of the life-continuum (bhavaṅgacalana) as an object appears at the mind-door, arrest of the life-continuum (bhavaṅgupaccheda) as that object appears, five-door adverting to the object present at both doors, eye-consciousness knowing visible form in dependence on the eye-base, receiving the object of eye-consciousness, investigating it, determining it, successive impulsions experiencing its flavour, and registration continuing with that same object.
paragraphs.M04-body-P135-S02: Past life-continuum. A visible object cannot appear at the eye-door and mind-door the instant it arises. It can appear only after one or several consciousness moments have passed. The life-continuum moments elapsed between its arising and its appearance at the two doors are called past life-continuum. Life-continuum before that object arises is marked separately. This does not imply that there are consciousness moments when no visible materiality arises at all, since materiality originated by kamma, consciousness, temperature or nutriment that includes visible form can generally arise during the arising, presence and dissolution of consciousness. Here the reference is only to the visible object capable of appearing at the eye-door and mind-door.

M04-body-P136.title: Eye-door processes ending in registration or impulsion
