M04-body-P148.title: How to apprehend eye-door and mind-door processes taking colour

paragraphs.M04-body-P148-S01:
To apprehend eye-door and mind-door processes arising with visible form as object, proceed as follows.
1. Re-establish a previously attained fourth-jhāna concentration in sequence.
2. Apprehend the two doors together so that they appear clearly: eye-sensitivity as the eye-door and the clear life-continuum as the mind-door.
3. Direct the mind to the colour of many material clusters or of a single cluster.
4. When that colour appears simultaneously at the eye-door and mind-door, an eye-door process arises and mind-door processes continue to take the same visible object.
5. Adverting, determining and mind-door adverting in those processes turn to and determine it simply as visible form, or colour. With wise attention, wholesome impulsions arise. The mentality in wholesome impulsion and registration, such as the set of thirty-four, belongs to the faith-and-wisdom group.
paragraphs.M04-body-P148-S02: One view holds that eye-door process mentality can take only the colour of many material clusters as object. A mind-door process can know the colour of one cluster or of many clusters. This is why both cases, the visible form of many clusters and of a single cluster, are stated here.

M04-body-P149.title: Limits of sense consciousness and the following mind-door process

paragraphs.M04-body-P149-S01:
Pañcahi viññāṇehi na kañci dhammaṃ paṭivijānāti aññatra abhinipātamattā. Pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ samanantarāpi na kañci dhammaṃ paṭivijānāti.
With the five consciousnesses one does not recognize any phenomenon beyond mere impingement. Immediately after the five consciousnesses one still does not recognize any phenomenon in that way (Abhidhamma, vol. 2, p. 123).
paragraphs.M04-body-P149-S02: According to this Pāli passage and the commentaries and subcommentaries on the Vibhaṅga, five-door process series with impulsion only know the meeting of door and object, namely the object coming before the respective door. They know only colour, sound, odour, taste or touch, and cannot yet distinguish white, red, yellow, blue and the like. Adverting and determining in the five-door process and mind-door adverting in the following mind-door process therefore cannot yet distinguish the object by such categories. That ability comes in later mind-door processes. The consciousnesses at adverting and determining in the five-door and following processes are called so because they operate in a way resembling decision.
paragraphs.M04-body-P149-S03: Practise seeing knowing consciousness in each moment: five-door adverting, eye-consciousness, receiving, investigating, determining, seven impulsions and two registrations. Many intervening life-continuum moments follow, then mind-door adverting, seven impulsions and two registrations…

M04-body-P150.title: Gradually increasing the number of mental factors apprehended

paragraphs.M04-body-P150-S01: Practise repeatedly, apprehending together the two doors, eye-sensitivity and the clear life-continuum, along with the visible object. When one eye-door process arises, many mind-door processes continue to take visible form, with many life-continuum moments between them. Practise until you distinguish these processes by wisdom. Once you can apprehend each process consciousness, add mental factors one by one, such as contact and feeling, in groups of two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, and so on. When you clearly see them arising together in each moment, discern consciousness and mental factors as set out in the table. You may begin from contact or feeling similarly. If not yet successful, repeatedly return to apprehending materiality. When the wisdom apprehending materiality becomes clear and free of confusion, mental phenomena naturally become clear to the meditator’s wisdom, as instructed in the Visuddhimagga (vol. 2, p. 223).
paragraphs.M04-body-P150-S02: Concrete and non-concrete materiality. In these processes eye-consciousness depends only on the eye-base, the medium-lived eye-sensitivity. The other mental phenomena in the eye-door and mind-door processes depend on the heart-base that arose with their respective immediately preceding consciousness. The table therefore also gives the supporting materiality. According to the method in the discourse, one must analyse with wisdom until compactness is broken down and apprehend ultimate materiality, so with regard to the base…

M04-body-P151.title: Supporting materiality, life-continuum, and wise attention

paragraphs.M04-body-P151-S01: … apprehend all discernible elemental and derived materiality together with the supporting materiality, rather than only bases such as the eye-base. The first part of the Majjhima Commentary (vol. 1, p. 281) and similar sources instruct apprehension in this way. The tables emphasize concrete materiality. At the stage of knowledge delimiting mentality and materiality, also apprehend any non-concrete materiality you can discern. At the insight stage set aside non-concrete materiality and discern concrete materiality alone.
paragraphs.M04-body-P151-S02: The table gives thirty-four life-continuum mental phenomena for a person with three-rooted rebirth-linking accompanied by joy. For a person with three-rooted rebirth-linking accompanied by equanimity, the life-continuum group contains thirty-three. Life-continuum takes just one of three objects: kamma, a kamma sign, or a destination sign, which appeared as the object of impulsion near death in the preceding existence. Once you can discern the past life-continuum object as indicated, include the life-continuum moments interspersed between the process series. At the beginning of apprehending mentality, if you cannot yet discern its actual object, you may temporarily set life-continuum mentality aside.
paragraphs.M04-body-P151-S03: Wise attention. 1. When discerning visible form, or colour, as visible form or colour, an eye-door process knowing colour arises, together with the following mind-door process and bare mind-door processes. The method of apprehension has already been given. Further, mind-door adverting in the mind-door process…

M04-body-P152.title: Ways of attending wisely to visible form

paragraphs.M04-body-P152-S01:
2. When discerning that visible object as materiality, apprehend the mind-door process consciousnesses that know it as materiality.
3. When taking its arising and passing away as object, seeing by wisdom and discerning it as impermanent, apprehend the mind-door process consciousnesses that know it as impermanent.
4. When taking its continual oppression by arising and passing away as object, seeing by wisdom and discerning it as suffering, apprehend the mind-door process consciousnesses that know it as suffering.
paragraphs.M04-body-P152-S02:
5. When taking its lack of an indestructible, enduring, permanent self with substance as object, seeing by wisdom and discerning that visible object as non-self, apprehend the mind-door process series that know it as non-self.
6. When taking its unattractive and repulsive nature through being mixed with unpleasant colours and smells as object, seeing by wisdom and discerning the visible object as unattractive, apprehend the mind-door process consciousnesses that know it as unattractive. Continue apprehending these mental phenomena.
paragraphs.M04-body-P152-S03: Eye-door process consciousnesses can know visible form only as visible form, or colour. They cannot know that colour as materiality, impermanent, suffering, non-self, or unattractive. Mind-door process consciousnesses can know that visible form as visible form or colour…

M04-body-P153.title: Why mentality is apprehended in six ways

paragraphs.M04-body-P153-S01: … or as materiality, impermanent, suffering, non-self, or unattractive.
paragraphs.M04-body-P153-S02: Apprehend the mentality taking visible form as object in six rounds to understand how wholesome impulsion arises through wise attention. Another reason is to prepare for insight practice, including comprehension by groups (kalāpasammasana) in the Visuddhimagga, vol. 2, pp. 260–264, and the sections on subsequent knowledges.
paragraphs.M04-body-P153-S03:
Ñātañca ñāṇañca ubhopi vipassati.
One discerns with insight both what is known and the knowledge (Visuddhimagga, vol. 2, p. 278).
paragraphs.M04-body-P153-S04: According to the determination of the ancient commentators, discern both with insight: what is known (ñāta), the phenomena of the truths of suffering and its origin to be penetrated by insight knowledge, and the knowledge (ñāṇa), the consciousness and mental factors in the mind-door process with insight impulsion, including the wisdom that discerns. Since the consciousness and mental factors in the insight process itself must also later be discerned, this prepares for discerning insight knowledge and its associated mentality. For these two reasons, apprehend the six rounds described above. Each round has four cases, twenty-four in all.
paragraphs.M04-body-P153-S05: Here too, according to the Sammohavinodanī commentary, registration cannot follow insight impulsions taking the characteristics of impermanence, suffering, and non-self of formations as object…

M04-body-P154.title: Registration after insight impulsion and the table of mental factors

paragraphs.M04-body-P154-S01: … and therefore some works omit registration after the insight impulsions knowing impermanence, suffering, and non-self. However, according to the Paṭṭhāna and commentary, registration still has an opportunity to occur after insight impulsions that are weak. Therefore, following insight impulsion, apprehend mentality according to the case with registration if it occurs, and according to the case without registration if it does not.
paragraphs.M04-body-P154-S02:
Counts of consciousness and mental factors
Five-door adverting | Eye-consciousness | Receiving | Investigating | Determining
11 | 8 | 11 | 12/11 | 12
1. Knowing consciousness | Knowing consciousness | Knowing consciousness | Knowing consciousness | Knowing consciousness
2. Contact | Contact | Contact | Contact | Contact
3. Feeling | Feeling | Feeling | Feeling | Feeling
4. Perception | Perception | Perception | Perception | Perception
5. Volition | Volition | Volition | Volition | Volition
6. One-pointedness | One-pointedness | One-pointedness | One-pointedness | One-pointedness
7. Life faculty | Life faculty | Life faculty | Life faculty | Life faculty
8. Attention | Attention | Attention | Attention | Attention
9. Applied thought |  | Applied thought | Applied thought | Applied thought
10. Sustained thought |  | Sustained thought | Sustained thought | Sustained thought
11. Decision |  | Decision | Decision | Decision
12 |  |  | Joy* | Energy

M04-body-P155.title: Explaining the mental counts in the eye-door process

paragraphs.M04-body-P155-S01: Five-door adverting has eleven instances of consciousness and mental factors and is always accompanied by equanimity. Eye-consciousness has eight and is always accompanied by equanimity. Receiving has eleven and is always accompanied by equanimity. Investigating accompanied by joyful feeling has twelve, because joy is present. In the second row investigating is accompanied by equanimity, so joy is absent and there are eleven. Determining has twelve and is always accompanied by equanimity.
paragraphs.M04-body-P155-S02: The thirty-four at impulsion are the thirty-four mental phenomena of the faith-and-wisdom group. 1. With knowledge and joy: thirty-four, accompanied by joyful feeling. 2. With knowledge and without joy: thirty-three, accompanied by equanimous feeling. 3. Without knowledge and with joy: thirty-three, accompanied by joyful feeling. 4. Without knowledge or joy: thirty-two, accompanied by equanimous feeling.
paragraphs.M04-body-P155-S03: For registration remember the four cases as for impulsion. However, when registration is rootless investigating accompanied by joy it has twelve instances of consciousness and mental factors. When investigating is accompanied by equanimity it has eleven. With an undesirable object it is unwholesome resultant, and with a desirable object it is wholesome resultant, as appropriate. If registration is great resultant, discern the same four cases as at impulsion.

M04-body-P156.title: Apprehending wholesome mentality taking sound as object

paragraphs.M04-body-P156-S01: Mind-door adverting is the same as determining and is accompanied by equanimous feeling.
paragraphs.M04-body-P156-S02: Note. Investigating, impulsion, and registration generally share the same kind of feeling. If impulsion is joyful, investigating and registration usually have joyful feeling. If impulsion is equanimous, they usually have equanimous feeling. With great wholesome impulsion, registration is usually great resultant. The table follows this general rule (see Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 1, pp. 130–131). The following briefly explains how to apprehend the sound group and the subsequent groups.
paragraphs.M04-body-P156-S03:
To seek and apprehend mentality in ear-door and mind-door processes with wholesome impulsion taking sound as object, proceed as follows.
1. If needed, re-establish your attained concentration in stages.
2. Apprehend together the ear-sensitivity, the ear-door, and the clear life-continuum, the mind-door.
paragraphs.M04-body-P156-S04:
3. Direct the mind to a sound you can hear, whether internal or external.
4. When the sound simultaneously impinges on, or comes before, the ear-door and mind-door, five-door adverting, ear-consciousness, receiving, investigating, determining, seven impulsions and two registrations arise. This is the ear-door process…

M04-body-P157.title: Six ways of attending to sound

paragraphs.M04-body-P157-S01: … followed by mind-door processes with mind-door adverting, seven impulsions and two registrations. Five-door adverting and determining, or mind-door adverting, attend to sound in the following ways. The first knows it as sound. The other five belong to mind-door adverting.
paragraphs.M04-body-P157-S02:
1. As sound.
2. As materiality.
3. As impermanent.
4. As suffering.
5. As non-self.
6. As unattractive.
paragraphs.M04-body-P157-S03: Discern each mode separately. With wise attention, wholesome impulsion arises. For each mode discern four cases, varying the presence or absence of knowledge and joy. This makes twenty-four rounds in all.
paragraphs.M04-body-P157-S04: Note. Re-establish concentration when needed. At the start of each sitting, re-establish concentration, up to fourth jhāna if possible. If one establishment allows continuous apprehension of mentality and materiality throughout the sitting, there is no need to repeat it. Repeat it only when apprehension becomes difficult. If you can apprehend continuously across all six groups beginning with visible form, continue. An adept may need to re-establish concentration only once per sitting.

M04-body-P158.title: Apprehending wholesome mentality taking odour as object

paragraphs.M04-body-P158-S01: Understand the same when apprehending mentality in the odour group and those that follow.
paragraphs.M04-body-P158-S02:
To seek and apprehend mentality in nose-door and mind-door processes with wholesome impulsion taking odour as object, proceed as follows.
1. If needed, re-establish your attained concentration in stages.
2. Apprehend together the nose-sensitivity, the nose-door, and the clear life-continuum, the mind-door.
paragraphs.M04-body-P158-S03: 3. Direct the mind to the odour of many material clusters or of a single cluster.
paragraphs.M04-body-P158-S04: 4. When odour impinges on, or appears before, the nose-door and mind-door simultaneously, the nose-door process arises with five-door adverting, nose-consciousness, receiving, investigating, determining, seven impulsions and two registrations. It is followed by mind-door processes with mind-door adverting, seven impulsions and two registrations, with many life-continuum moments between processes.
paragraphs.M04-body-P158-S05: Five-door adverting and determining, or mind-door adverting, know the odour: 1. As odour. 2. As materiality. 3. As impermanent. 4. As suffering…

M04-body-P159.title: Apprehending wholesome mentality taking taste as object

paragraphs.M04-body-P159-S02: Discern each mode separately. With wise attention, wholesome impulsion arises. For each mode discern four cases, varying the presence or absence of knowledge and joy. This makes twenty-four rounds in all.
paragraphs.M04-body-P159-S03:
To seek and apprehend mentality in tongue-door and mind-door processes with wholesome impulsion taking taste as object, proceed as follows.
1. If needed, re-establish your attained concentration in stages.
2. Apprehend together the tongue-sensitivity, the tongue-door, and the clear life-continuum, the mind-door.
paragraphs.M04-body-P159-S04: 3. Direct the mind to the taste of many material clusters or of a single cluster.
paragraphs.M04-body-P159-S05: 4. When taste impinges on, or appears before, the tongue-door and mind-door simultaneously, the tongue-door process arises with five-door adverting, tongue-consciousness, receiving, investigating, determining, seven impulsions and two registrations. It is followed by mind-door processes with mind-door adverting, seven impulsions and two registrations, with many life-continuum moments between processes.
paragraphs.M04-body-P159-S06: One tongue-door process may be followed by many mind-door processes. Five-door adverting and determining, or mind-door adverting, attend in the following ways.

M04-body-P160.title: Six ways of attending to taste and beginning to discern tangibles

paragraphs.M04-body-P160-S01:
1. As taste.
2. As materiality.
3. As impermanent.
4. As suffering.
5. As non-self.
6. As unattractive.
paragraphs.M04-body-P160-S02: Discern each mode separately. With wise attention, wholesome impulsion arises. For each mode discern four cases, varying the presence or absence of knowledge and joy. This makes twenty-four rounds in all.
paragraphs.M04-body-P160-S03:
To seek and apprehend mentality in body-door and mind-door processes with wholesome impulsion taking tangibles as object, proceed as follows.
1. If needed, re-establish your attained concentration in stages.
2. Apprehend together the body-sensitivity, the body-door, and the clear life-continuum, the mind-door.
paragraphs.M04-body-P160-S04: 3. Direct the mind to the tangible object of many material clusters or of a single cluster. It is the tangible object in the material clusters immediately adjoining the body-sensitivity, the body-door you are apprehending.

paragraphs.M04-body-P161-S01: There are three kinds of tangible object. Take one of the three elements, earth, fire, or wind, as object and discern it.
paragraphs.M04-body-P161-S02: 4. When the tangible object impinges on, or appears before, the body-door and mind-door simultaneously, the body-door process arises with five-door adverting, body-consciousness, receiving, investigating, determining, seven impulsions and two registrations. It is followed by mind-door processes with mind-door adverting, seven impulsions and two registrations, with many life-continuum moments between processes.
paragraphs.M04-body-P161-S03: One body-door process may be followed by many mind-door processes. Five-door adverting and determining, or mind-door adverting, know the object in the following six ways.
paragraphs.M04-body-P161-S04:
1. As a tangible object, namely the earth, fire, or wind element.
2. As materiality.
3. As impermanent.
4. As suffering.
5. As non-self.
6. As unattractive.
paragraphs.M04-body-P161-S05: Discern the six modes separately for each element: six rounds for earth, six for fire, and six for wind. Within each discern the four cases with and without knowledge and joy. The total is 3 × 6 × 4 = 72 rounds.

paragraphs.M04-body-P162-S01: Here meditators may test for themselves whether the brain contains the wisdom called the wisdom faculty. According to the Buddha’s Abhidhamma, the brain is a collection of material clusters. Attend closely to the four elements in the brain. The minute material clusters soon become easy to see, since the five kinds of cluster and forty-four kinds of materiality in the brain were already apprehended in the section on materiality. Apprehend those forty-four again, then select and apprehend body-sensitivity.
paragraphs.M04-body-P162-S02:
1. Apprehend body-sensitivity, the body-door, and the clear life-continuum, the mind-door.
2. Apprehend together with them one of the elements of earth, fire, or wind in one or many clusters next to that body-sensitivity.
paragraphs.M04-body-P162-S03: When such a tangible object comes before and appears simultaneously at the two doors, the body-sensitivity in the brain and the clear life-continuum, body-door process consciousnesses and mind-door process series with impulsion arise taking that same tangible object. In those processes…

paragraphs.M04-body-P163-S01: … if determining and mind-door adverting attend wisely, determining the object as earth, fire, wind, materiality, impermanent and the like, processes with great wholesome impulsion arise. Each impulsion moment contains thirty-four mental phenomena with knowledge and joy, or thirty-three with knowledge and without joy. These sets of thirty-four or thirty-three arise depending on the heart-base, with the clear life-continuum as door. They include wisdom called the wisdom faculty. Body-consciousness dependent on body-sensitivity in the brain, however, can arise only with the seven universal mental factors, eight mental phenomena altogether. Those eight do not include wisdom. Practise repeatedly to verify this statement yourself.
paragraphs.M04-body-P163-S02: Note. With a desirable tangible object, body-consciousness is accompanied by pleasant bodily feeling. With an undesirable object, it is accompanied by painful bodily feeling. Apprehend this until it is clear. Beyond body-consciousness, apprehend the distinct feelings, such as joy and equanimity, in each process moment across all six groups.
paragraphs.M04-body-P163-S03: This completes the explanation of apprehending the wholesome-group mentality with wholesome impulsion in the six domains: visible form, sound, odour, taste, tangibles, and mind objects. When you have become adept at apprehending the mentality associated with wholesome impulsion in all six groups…

M04-body-P164.title: Four mind-object groups and immaterial jhāna mentality

paragraphs.M04-body-P164-S01: … apprehend them in sequence from visible form to mind objects. For ease of recollection, the processes with wholesome impulsion taking mind objects are divided into four groups.
paragraphs.M04-body-P164-S02:
a. Mentality discerned taking ten or eleven concrete material phenomena as objects.
b. Mentality discerned taking ten non-concrete material phenomena as objects.
c. Mentality of abstinence, immeasurable factors, recollection of the Buddha, and recollection of death.
d. Jhāna mentality.
paragraphs.M04-body-P164-S03: This concludes apprehending mentality in the group with wholesome impulsion. If you have developed the ten kasiṇas and eight attainments, proceed to apprehend mentality in those attainments. The four immaterial jhānas have only two factors, equanimity and one-pointedness. With applied thought, sustained thought, and joy absent, each has thirty-one mental phenomena.
paragraphs.M04-body-P164-S04:
1. To apprehend the mentality of the base of infinite space, apprehend together the mind-door and the conceptual object of infinite space, then seek and apprehend the jhāna mentality.
2. To apprehend the mentality of the base of infinite consciousness, apprehend the mind-door together with its object, the consciousness of the base of infinite space…

M04-body-P165.title: Objects of the remaining immaterial jhānas

paragraphs.M04-body-P165-S01:
… then seek and apprehend the jhāna mentality.
3. To apprehend the mentality of the base of nothingness, apprehend together the mind-door and the conceptual object “there is nothing”, the absence of the consciousness of the base of infinite space, then seek and apprehend the jhāna mentality.
4. To apprehend the mentality of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, apprehend together the mind-door and its object, the jhāna of the base of nothingness, then seek and apprehend the jhāna mentality.
paragraphs.M04-body-P165-S02: The following explains how to seek and apprehend mentality in the unwholesome group, with unwholesome impulsion.

paragraphs.M04-body-P166-S01: Does discerning unwholesome phenomena make more unwholesomeness arise? Many meditators ask this. In answer, the Buddha teaches in the Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna Sutta:
paragraphs.M04-body-P166-S02:
Sarāgaṃ vā cittaṃ sarāgaṃ cittanti pajānāti, vītarāgaṃ vā cittaṃ vītarāgaṃ cittanti pajānāti.
One understands a mind with lust as a mind with lust, and a mind free from lust as a mind free from lust (Majjhima Nikāya, vol. 1, p. 56).
paragraphs.M04-body-P166-S03: When told that the Buddha himself teaches discerning a mind with lust and a mind free from lust in this way, some think the instruction means only to discern lust, hatred, and delusion when they arise of themselves. No conditioned phenomenon arises on its own at will. Conditioned phenomena can arise only when their respective conditions come together and operate. Among the conditions for those conditioned phenomena…

paragraphs.M04-body-P167-S01: … unwise attention is the nearest condition for unwholesome impulsion. When one encounters an object and attends to it in the wrong way, unwholesome impulsions arise as appropriate. Beings also tend to relish unwholesome phenomena. They take pride in loving a son, delight in loving a daughter, and love grandchildren so much they cannot bear to be parted. They relish their own unwholesomeness again, thinking, “My greed is different from others’ greed, my aversion is different from others’ aversion.” Earlier instances of greed or aversion condition later ones. Greed, aversion and such unwholesome phenomena therefore also need to be discerned with insight. If this is unclear, read the following commentary.
paragraphs.M04-body-P167-S02:
Tattha yogāvacaro kāmavitakkassa padaghātanatthaṃ kāmavitakkaṃ vā sammasati aññaṃ vā kiñci saṅkhāraṃ. Athassa vipassanākkhaṇe vipassanāsampayutto saṅkappo tadaṅgavasena kāmavitakkassa padaghātaṃ padacchedaṃ karonto uppajjati. Vipassanaṃ ussukkāpetvā maggaṃ pāpeti. Athassa maggakkhaṇe maggasampayutto saṅkappo samucchedavasena kāmavitakkassa padaghātaṃ padacchedaṃ karonto uppajjati. Byāpādavitakkassāpi padaghātanatthaṃ byāpādavitakkaṃ vā aññaṃ vā saṅkhāraṃ, vihiṃsāvitakkassa padaghātanatthaṃ vihiṃsāvitakkaṃ vā aññaṃ vā saṅkhāraṃ sammasati. Athassa vipassanākkhaṇeti sabbaṃ purimanayeneva yojetabbaṃ.
Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 2, p. 100. The explanation continues on Burmese pages 168–169.

M04-body-P168.title: Discerning three kinds of unwholesome thought

paragraphs.M04-body-P168-S01: There are three unwholesome thoughts: sensual thought, thought of ill will, and thought of harming. To abandon the conditions for sensual thought, thinking and planning about sensuality, the meditator discerns sensual thought or some other formation by one of the three characteristics, impermanence, suffering, and non-self. While discerning, applied thought called right intention arises associated with insight knowledge. Through abandonment by substitution of opposites (tadaṅgappahāna), it strikes down and cuts off the conditions for sensual thought. The meditator strives to bring insight to the noble path. At the path moment, right intention associated with the noble path arises, striking down and cutting off the conditions for sensual thought through eradication (samucchedappahāna).
paragraphs.M04-body-P168-S02: To abandon the conditions for thought of ill will, thinking and planning to destroy beings, discern thought of ill will or another formation by the three characteristics. To abandon the conditions for thought of harming, thinking and planning to cause beings pain, discern thought of harming or another formation by the three characteristics. While discerning in this way…

M04-body-P169.title: Abandoning unwholesome thought by substitution and eradication

paragraphs.M04-body-P169-S01: … in the meditator’s continuum, when insight knowledge arises, applied thought called right intention associated with that knowledge arises, striking down and cutting off conditions for ill will and harming through abandonment by substitution of opposites. The meditator strives through the sequence of insight knowledges up to the noble path. At the noble path moment, right intention associated with the path arises, striking down and cutting off the conditions for ill will and harming through eradication (Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 2, p. 100).
paragraphs.M04-body-P169-S02: Sensual thought is applied thought associated with greed-rooted consciousness and its mental factors. Ill will and harming are applied thought associated with hatred-rooted consciousness and its mental factors. Discern the greed-rooted groups with sensual thought and the hatred-rooted groups with ill will or harming by the three characteristics. Also discern the other formations. During insight, insight knowledge, or the right intention associated with it, abandons those unwholesome thoughts by substitution of opposites. The noble path arising at the culmination of mature insight eradicates them. This is the meaning of the commentary above.
paragraphs.M04-body-P169-S03: Thus, discerning unwholesome phenomena with insight serves to abandon them by substitution and by eradication…

M04-body-P170.title: Four cases of the greed-and-wrong-view group

paragraphs.M04-body-P170-S01: … Understand that the purpose of that discernment is to abandon the unwholesome. First, the following presents the groups of unwholesome mentality that commonly arise.
paragraphs.M04-body-P170-S02:
Greed and wrong view
Component | Count
Knowing consciousness | 1
Ethically variable mental factors | 13
Universal unwholesome mental factors | 4
Greed and wrong view | 2
Total | 20
paragraphs.M04-body-P170-S03:
Four cases associated with wrong view
Case | Mental phenomena
1. Joyful, unprompted | 20
2. Equanimous, unprompted, without joy | 19
3. Joyful, prompted | 20 + sloth and torpor = 22
4. Equanimous, prompted | 19 + sloth and torpor = 21
paragraphs.M04-body-P170-S04: In these groups, joyful feeling occurs with joy, while equanimous feeling does not. Energy here is the particular effort for greed and wrong view to arise. Desire is the wish for greed and wrong view to arise…

M04-body-P171.title: The greed-and-conceit group and the hatred group

paragraphs.M04-body-P171-S01: … In other words, energy is striving for greed to arise, while desire is wanting greed to arise. The remaining mental factors may be understood by their respective natures.
paragraphs.M04-body-P171-S02: The greed-and-conceit group has four cases. Substitute conceit for wrong view in the greed-and-wrong-view group, and the counts remain twenty, nineteen, twenty-two and twenty-one. Conceit is an occasional mental factor and is sometimes absent. When neither conceit nor wrong view occurs, the counts are nineteen, eighteen, twenty-one and twenty respectively. Discern these four cases. Four consciousnesses associated with wrong view and four dissociated from it make eight greed-rooted consciousnesses.
paragraphs.M04-body-P171-S03:
Two cases of the hatred group
Component | Count
Knowing consciousness | 1
Ethically variable mental factors, excluding joy | 12
Universal unwholesome mental factors | 4
Hatred | 1
Unprompted total | 18
Prompted, adding sloth and torpor | 20

M04-body-P172.title: Hatred with envy, stinginess, or remorse

paragraphs.M04-body-P172-S01:
Hatred and envy
Component | Count
Mental phenomena of the hatred group | 18
Envy | 1
Unprompted total | 19
Prompted, adding sloth and torpor | 21
paragraphs.M04-body-P172-S02:
Hatred and stinginess
Component | Count
Mental phenomena of the hatred group | 18
Stinginess | 1
Unprompted total | 19
Prompted, adding sloth and torpor | 21
paragraphs.M04-body-P172-S03:
Hatred and remorse
Component | Count
Mental phenomena of the hatred group | 18
Remorse | 1
Unprompted total | 19
Prompted, adding sloth and torpor | 21
paragraphs.M04-body-P172-S04: For remorse, take misconduct already done as object and discern the unprompted and prompted cases. Take good conduct that should have been done but was omitted as object and discern the unprompted and prompted cases. This completes the discernment of the two hatred-rooted consciousnesses. The following deals with the two delusion-rooted consciousnesses.

paragraphs.M04-body-P173-S01:
Delusion and restlessness
Component | Count
Knowing consciousness | 1
Universal mental factors | 7
Applied thought, sustained thought, decision and energy. Joy and desire are absent. | 4
Universal unwholesome mental factors | 4
Total | 16
paragraphs.M04-body-P173-S02:
Delusion and doubt
Component | Count
Knowing consciousness | 1
Universal mental factors | 7
Applied thought, sustained thought and energy. Decision, joy and desire are absent. | 3
Universal unwholesome mental factors | 4
Doubt | 1
Total | 16
paragraphs.M04-body-P173-S03: This completes the discernment of the two delusion-rooted consciousnesses. Eight rooted in greed, two rooted in hatred, and two rooted in delusion make twelve unwholesome consciousnesses to discern. According to the analysis of processes in the Abhidhammatthasaṅgaha and Abhidhamma teachings such as the Dhammasaṅgaṇī, all twenty-nine sense-sphere impulsions can occur in five-door processes such as the eye-door process, and in mind-door processes. These include twelve unwholesome impulsions. The Buddha himself also teaches discerning a mind with lust accompanied by lust…

M04-body-P174.title: Beginning from ultimate materiality or a conceptual object

paragraphs.M04-body-P174-S01: … a mind with hatred accompanied by hatred and a mind with delusion accompanied by delusion, in the contemplation of mind in the Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna Sutta.
paragraphs.M04-body-P174-S02:
Tasmā taṃ rūpaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā uppannaṃ vedanaṃ saññaṃ saṅkhāre viññāṇañca “idaṃ arūpan”ti vavatthapetvā aniccādito passati.
Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 1, p. 128. Beginners in the meditation on mentality first apprehend the mentality arising with each of the twenty-eight material phenomena as object. Seek and apprehend all twenty-eight. Classified by object, there are six kinds. First comes mentality arising with each of the ten or eleven concrete and ten non-concrete material phenomena belonging to the mind-object domain.
paragraphs.M04-body-P174-S03: Some meditators may find it difficult to discern the individual groups of unwholesome phenomena arising with an ultimate material phenomenon as object. If so, begin with unwholesome groups arising with particular conceptual objects already familiar to you. This is easier because the mind of one who has yet to develop knowledge of ultimate reality generally operates within the sphere of concepts. Just as when watering a tree, to learn the method more easily also practise discerning mentality arising with concepts as objects, as when directing water into a channel…

M04-body-P175.title: Example of the greed-and-wrong-view group taking gold as object

paragraphs.M04-body-P175-S01: … and thereby understand unwholesome phenomena. For these two purposes, those who encounter difficulty may begin by apprehending mentality arising with a concept as object. They may also discern directly with ultimate materiality as object. Once they can apprehend unwholesome mentality taking ultimate materiality as object, they need not repeat the exercise with conceptual objects. An example follows for those whose discernment is still weak, using mentality in a mind-door process with unwholesome impulsion taking a concept as object.
paragraphs.M04-body-P175-S02:
The greed-and-wrong-view group.
1. If needed, re-establish concentration.
2. Apprehend the clear life-continuum, the mind-door.
3. Direct the mind to gold, for example gold you own and like.
4. When gold appears at the mind-door, series of mind-door processes with impulsion arise taking a particular conceptual object, gold, as object. Mind-door adverting in those processes turns towards and determines it as “gold”. Attend unwisely. The unwholesome impulsion group with greed and wrong view will then arise.

M04-body-P176.title: Wrong view taking gold and familiar things as objects

paragraphs.M04-body-P176-S01: When this process takes a concept as object, registration has no opportunity to occur. If, instead of the concept “gold”, one takes as object the colour of the many material clusters in it, registration has an opportunity to occur.
paragraphs.M04-body-P176-S02: In the unwholesome impulsion group with greed and wrong view, misapprehending it as “gold” belongs to delusion, while believing in and holding to “gold” belongs to wrong view. This is one kind of worldly convention. Understand the remaining factors by their natures. Likewise try determining that lump of gold as permanent, pleasant, self, or beautiful. Unwholesome processes of the greed-and-wrong-view group occur similarly. In these mental phenomena, misapprehension as permanent, pleasant, self, and attractive is delusion, while belief in and adherence to those views is wrong view. Understand and discern clothing similarly. Discern clearly how joy often arises for a new garment or robe but does not arise for an old one.
paragraphs.M04-body-P176-S03: Misapprehension and adherence to permanence here take forms such as “Yesterday it was my gold and today it is still my gold. Yesterday it was my garment or robe and today it is still mine. Yesterday he was my son and today he is still my son.” If someone says, “That is not your gold, garment, robe, or son,” one who has yet to discern ultimate reality and is clinging will find this hard to accept. Understand the nature of these phenomena through such misapprehension and adherence.

M04-body-P177.title: Objects for the greed-and-conceit group and hatred groups

paragraphs.M04-body-P177-S01: Greed and conceit. Conceit is the wish to surpass others and stand above them. One considers one’s own animate or inanimate sensual possessions superior to those of others and of a higher order, exalts oneself and takes pride. Take a familiar object concerning which you wish to compete or excel, such as clothing, houses, cars, sons, or wives. Apprehend the mind-door together with it and discern. Once you understand the greed-and-wrong-view or greed-and-conceit group with concepts as objects, discern with ultimate materiality as object.
paragraphs.M04-body-P177-S02: Hatred-rooted groups. 1. For hatred, take a person you habitually dislike or an object that provokes hatred. 2. For hatred and envy, take another’s possession that surpasses yours. 3. For hatred and stinginess, take one of your own animate or inanimate sensual possessions that you do not want another to have. 4. For hatred and remorse, take misconduct already done, such as an occasion of killing, or good conduct omitted, such as failing to carry out an act of giving or observe virtue.

M04-body-P178.title: Objects of remorse, restlessness, and doubt

paragraphs.M04-body-P178-S01: Remorse is later distress at misconduct already done, so that misconduct can be taken as object for discernment. It is also distress at having omitted good conduct, so that omission too can be taken as object. Extend the discernment according to your wisdom. Many meditators find this group difficult to discern with ultimate materiality as object.
paragraphs.M04-body-P178-S02: Delusion-rooted groups. For delusion and restlessness, first discern a familiar conceptual object that makes the mind wander without greed or hatred. For delusion and doubt, take an object liable to stir doubt, for example, “Was there really a previous life?”
paragraphs.M04-body-P178-S03: When discerning concepts in this way, registration does not follow unwholesome mind-door impulsion. If one can take ultimate materiality such as colour, sound or odour as object, registration has an opportunity to arise. Once you have apprehended unwholesome mentality taking concepts as objects, proceed to apprehend unwholesome mentality taking each kind of ultimate materiality as object. As with the processes with wholesome impulsion, begin with the mind-object group.

M04-body-P179.title: Twenty mental phenomena in the greed-and-wrong-view group

paragraphs.M04-body-P179-S01: For those whose discernment is still weak, the twenty mental phenomena in the greed-and-wrong-view group arising with eye-sensitivity as object are presented again. Understand the other groups of unwholesome mentality on the same model.
paragraphs.M04-body-P179-S02:
1. Knowing consciousness. Apprehending eye-sensitivity as object.
2. Contact (phassa). Touching eye-sensitivity and connecting it with knowing consciousness. Note: “object” in the following entries means eye-sensitivity.
3. Feeling (vedanā). Experiencing the flavour of the object, here with joyful feeling.
4. Perception (saññā). Marking the object as beautiful. Understand similarly when marking it as permanent, pleasant or self.
5. Volition (cetanā). Prompting and urging the associated phenomena towards the object.
6. One-pointedness (ekaggatā). Placing the mind on a single object and keeping the associated phenomena from scattering away from it.

M04-body-P180.title: Mental factors from life faculty to delusion

paragraphs.M04-body-P180-S01:
7. Life faculty (jīvita). Sustaining associated phenomena on the object.
8. Attention (manasikāra). Directing and driving consciousness and associated phenomena towards the object, bringing the object to mind.
9. Applied thought (vitakka). Placing consciousness and associated phenomena on the object, thinking about it.
10. Sustained thought (vicāra). Continually examining and rubbing against the object, taking it again and again.
11. Decision (adhimokkha). Deciding that the object is beautiful. Understand similarly when deciding it to be permanent, pleasant or self.
paragraphs.M04-body-P180-S02:
12. Energy (viriya). Striving for greed, wrong view, and similar unwholesome phenomena to arise in relation to the object.
13. Joy (pīti). Taking delight in the object.
14. Desire (chanda). Wanting the object, that is, wanting greed to arise.
15. Delusion (moha). Failing to know the object’s truly unattractive nature. Understand its truly impermanent, suffering and non-self nature similarly. Delusion also misapprehends the object as beautiful. Understand similarly when misapprehending it as permanent, pleasant or self.

M04-body-P181.title: The remaining factors and four cases of the greed group

paragraphs.M04-body-P181-S01:
16. Lack of moral shame (ahirika). Lack of shame at greed, wrong view, and similar unwholesome phenomena arising in relation to the object.
17. Lack of moral dread (anottappa). Lack of fear of such unwholesome phenomena arising in relation to the object.
18. Restlessness (uddhacca). The mind is unsettled and agitated in relation to the object.
19. Greed (lobha). Appropriating the object as “mine”, wanting and becoming infatuated with it, clinging to it.
20. Wrong view (diṭṭhi). Holding and believing the object to be beautiful, misconstruing and misjudging it in that way. Understand similarly when it is held to be permanent, pleasant or self.
paragraphs.M04-body-P181-S02: Feeling, joy, sloth and torpor. Greed-rooted consciousness accompanied by joyful feeling has joy. When accompanied by equanimous feeling it lacks joy. Unprompted consciousness lacks sloth and torpor, while prompted consciousness can have them. Discern four cases according to whether joy, sloth and torpor are associated.
paragraphs.M04-body-P181-S03: Energy and desire. In each of the groups of hatred, hatred and envy, hatred and stinginess, and hatred and remorse, energy is the particular effort for those respective phenomena to arise. Desire is wanting them to arise.

M04-body-P182.title: Delusion, lack of shame, and lack of dread in the unwholesome groups

paragraphs.M04-body-P182-S01: Delusion misapprehends eye-sensitivity and similar objects as permanent, pleasant, self, or attractive, or misapprehends them in such terms as “another’s eye-sensitivity” or “my eye-sensitivity”.
paragraphs.M04-body-P182-S02: Lack of moral shame and lack of moral dread are being unashamed and unafraid of the arising of such unwholesome phenomena as greed and wrong view, greed and conceit, hatred, hatred and envy, hatred and stinginess, hatred and remorse, delusion and restlessness, and delusion and doubt. When apprehending mentality arising while committing misconduct, the absence of shame and dread at that moment concerns the very misconduct being committed.
paragraphs.M04-body-P182-S03: For unwholesome mentality arising with the remaining nine or ten concrete material phenomena and the ten non-concrete material phenomena in the mind-object group, discern using eye-sensitivity as the model. First comes the table of mind-door processes with unwholesome impulsion.

M04-body-P183.title: Mind-door process table for unwholesome impulsion taking mind objects

paragraphs.M04-body-P183-S01:
Unwholesome group taking mind objects. Supporting materiality in the heart: 54.
Group | Mind-door adverting | Impulsion (7) | Rootless registration (2) | Rooted registration (2)
1. Greed and wrong view | 12 | 20 (19/22/21) | 12 (11/12/11) (8) | 34/33/33/32
2. Greed and conceit | 12 | 20 (19/22/21) | 12 (11/12/11) | 34/33/33/32
3. Hatred | 12 | 18 (20) | 11 (11) | 33/32
4. Hatred and envy | 12 | 19 (21) | 11 (11) | 33/32
5. Hatred and stinginess | 12 | 19 (21) | 11 (11) | 33/32
6. Hatred and remorse | 12 | 19 (21) | 11 (11) | 33/32
7. Restlessness | 12 | 16 | 12 (11/11) | 34/33/33/32
8. Doubt | 12 | 16 | 12 (11/11) | 34/33/33/32

M04-body-P184.title: Discerning greed and wrong view with eye-sensitivity as object

paragraphs.M04-body-P184-S01:
1. If needed, re-establish concentration in stages.
2. Apprehend the clear life-continuum, the mind-door.
3. Analyse the eye-decad and direct the mind to eye-sensitivity.
4. When eye-sensitivity appears before the mind-door, mind-door process series with impulsion arise taking it as object. Mind-door adverting in these processes determines it to be beautiful. Even when that eye-sensitivity is desirable, unwise attention gives rise to greed-and-wrong-view mentality at impulsion, delighting and clinging on account of regarding it as beautiful. Wrong attention, attending as beautiful, is among the nearest conditions for greed impulsion.
paragraphs.M04-body-P184-S02: Understand similarly when determining and attending to eye-sensitivity as permanent, pleasant, or self. Of eight greed-rooted consciousnesses four are associated with wrong view. Joy is present with joyful feeling and absent with equanimity. Prompted means with inducement, so sloth and torpor may be present. Unprompted means without inducement, so they are absent. Inducement is prompting oneself or being prompted by another for greed, hatred, or similar unwholesome phenomena to arise. The counts of consciousness and mental factors in each moment of the process series are given in the table.

M04-body-P185.title: Discerning conceit, hatred, envy, and stinginess with eye-sensitivity

paragraphs.M04-body-P185-S01: In the greed-and-conceit group, conceit is occasional and is associated only when conditions are present. When neither conceit nor wrong view is associated, the respective counts of consciousness and mental factors at impulsion are nineteen, eighteen, twenty-one, and twenty. There are four cases according to joyful or equanimous feeling and prompted or unprompted occurrence.
paragraphs.M04-body-P185-S02: Greed and conceit taking eye-sensitivity. Apprehend the mind-door together with eye-sensitivity and try attending, “I have obtained this eye-sensitivity.” Mind-door process series with unwholesome impulsion in which greed and conceit predominate will arise. Break down the compactness of mentality and apprehend ultimate mental phenomena.
paragraphs.M04-body-P185-S03:
Hatred. Take as object undesirable eye-sensitivity that was once impaired. Apprehend the mind-door together with the mental phenomena of the hatred group.
Hatred and envy. Take another’s eye-sensitivity that surpasses your own, that is, eyes more beautiful than yours, and attend, “If only that person did not have such eye-sensitivity”, or “If only that person did not have such eyes”. Mentality in which hatred and envy predominate will arise. Apprehend it down to ultimate reality.
Hatred and stinginess. Take your own eye-sensitivity that you do not want others to encroach upon. You may take as object your unwillingness to bear it when someone scoffs, “What is so beautiful about your eyes?”

M04-body-P186.title: Discerning remorse, restlessness and doubt, and the rule for registration

paragraphs.M04-body-P186-S01:
Hatred and remorse. Take as object a wrong thing said or done in connection with eye-sensitivity. Alternatively, take the later distress over failing to do something that should have been done in connection with eye-sensitivity.
Delusion and restlessness. If the mind has been agitated in relation to eye-sensitivity, discern with that same object in the absence of greed and hatred.
Delusion and doubt. Discern with the question, “Is this eye-sensitivity the sensitivity of a self?” This follows the arising of the ten fetters with visible form as object as explained in the commentary. See Dīgha Commentary, vol. 2, p. 377, and Majjhima Commentary, vol. 1, p. 292. This will be explained below.
paragraphs.M04-body-P186-S02: Registration. The table shows both rootless and rooted registration. Both kinds should not be understood to arise in the same process. Either one rootless kind or one rooted kind can occur as appropriate. Of the eleven kinds of registration, only one can occur in a process. Impulsion and registration generally have the same feeling. If impulsion has joyful feeling, registration also has joyful feeling. When joy is associated with impulsion, it is associated with registration. If impulsion has equanimous feeling, registration has equanimous feeling. If impulsion lacks joy, registration lacks it too. However, if impulsion is accompanied by displeasure, registration cannot have displeasure and can only have equanimity. Thus after hatred impulsion only equanimous registration has an opportunity to occur. As the preceding table shows…

M04-body-P187.title: Alternating discernment of wholesome and unwholesome groups

paragraphs.M04-body-P187-S01: … great-resultant registration can also follow unwholesome impulsion as appropriate. For instance, with an exceptionally desirable object such as the Buddha, unwise attention can give rise to unwholesome impulsion, which can also be followed by great-resultant registration as appropriate. Hence the table shows both rootless and rooted registration. Meditators will understand through practice.
paragraphs.M04-body-P187-S02: For unwholesome mentality taking the remaining concrete and non-concrete material phenomena in the mind-object domain as objects, follow the model of eye-sensitivity.
paragraphs.M04-body-P187-S03: A way to practise. From observing many meditators, when they devote a whole sitting to apprehending only processes with unwholesome impulsion, the mind sometimes becomes clouded and the light gradually dims. Having learned to apprehend wholesome processes, it is better to alternate wholesome and unwholesome processes. For instance, after apprehending wholesome mind-door processes with eye-sensitivity as object, continue with unwholesome mind-door processes taking that same eye-sensitivity as object, determining the same object…

M04-body-P188.title: How the ten fetters arise on seeing visible form

paragraphs.M04-body-P188-S01: … If the wholesome and unwholesome groups that arise with each kind of materiality are apprehended in turn like this, the mind usually does not become clouded and the light does not fade.
paragraphs.M04-body-P188-S02: Next comes apprehending mentality in five-door and mind-door processes with unwholesome impulsion taking the five objects beginning with visible form. Before apprehending it, learn how the ten fetters arise as explained in the commentaries.
paragraphs.M04-body-P188-S03:
Cakkhudvāre tāva āpāthagataṃ iṭṭhārammaṇaṃ kāmassādavasena assādayato abhinandato kāmarāgasaṃyojanaṃ uppajjati. Aniṭṭhārammaṇe kujjhato paṭighasaṃyojanaṃ uppajjati. “Ṭhapetvā maṃ na koci añño etaṃ ārammaṇaṃ vibhāvetuṃ samattho atthī”ti maññato mānasaṃyojanaṃ uppajjati. “Etaṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ niccaṃ dhuvan”ti gaṇhato diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ uppajjati. “Etaṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ satto nu kho, sattassa nu kho”ti vicikicchato vicikicchāsaṃyojanaṃ uppajjati. “Sampattibhave vata no idaṃ sulabhaṃ jātan”ti bhavaṃ patthentassa bhavarāgasaṃyojanaṃ uppajjati. “Āyatimpi evarūpaṃ sīlabbataṃ samādiyitvā sakkā laddhun”ti sīlabbataṃ samādiyantassa sīlabbataparāmāsasaṃyojanaṃ uppajjati. “Aho vata etaṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ aññe na labheyyun”ti usūyato issāsaṃyojanaṃ uppajjati. Attanā laddhaṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ aññassa maccharāyato macchariyasaṃyojanaṃ uppajjati. Sabbeheva sahajātaaññāṇavasena avijjāsaṃyojanaṃ uppajjati.
Dīgha Commentary, vol. 2, p. 377. Majjhima Commentary, vol. 1, p. 292. The translation and explanation of each fetter follow.

M04-body-P189.title: The fetters of sensual desire and desire for existence

paragraphs.M04-body-P189-S01:
Niccaṃ dhuvanti etaṃ nidassanamattaṃ. “Ucchijjissati vinassissatī”ti gaṇhatoti evamādīnampi saṅgaho icchitabbo. Bhavaṃ patthentassāti “īdise sampattibhave yasmā amhākaṃ idaṃ iṭṭhārammaṇaṃ sulabhaṃ jātaṃ, tasmā āyatimpi sampattibhavo bhaveyyā”ti bhavaṃ nikāmentassa. Evarūpaṃ sakkā laddhunti yojanā.
“Permanent, enduring” is an example only. Views such as “it will be cut off and perish” are also included. One who longs for existence wishes for a prosperous existence in the future, thinking that an agreeable object is easily obtained in such an existence. The passage is construed as saying that such an object can be obtained. (Majjhima Subcommentary, vol. 1, p. 379.)
paragraphs.M04-body-P189-S02: Of the twenty-eight material phenomena, the Dīgha Commentary, Mahāvagga (vol. 2, p. 377), and the Majjhima Commentary, Mūlapaṇṇāsa (vol. 1, p. 292), explain the arising of the ten fetters with visible form as object in the section on the bases in the Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna Sutta. By understanding visible form, you can understand and apprehend how they arise with the remaining twenty-seven material phenomena. The commentaries also explain the ten fetters by the Abhidhamma method. Here they are presented in order of greed-, hatred-, and delusion-rooted consciousness to facilitate discernment and recollection.
paragraphs.M04-body-P189-S03: 1. The fetter of sensual desire. When a desirable, agreeable and prized visible object appears before the eye-door and mind-door, the fetter of sensual desire arises in the continuum of one who regards it as beautiful and relishes it for the gratification of sensuality. This fetter is craving, greed associated with the eight greed-rooted consciousnesses, both with and without wrong view, clinging to animate or inanimate sensual objects.
paragraphs.M04-body-P189-S04: 2. The fetter of desire for existence. This fetter arises in the continuum of one who longs for a prosperous existence, thinking, “Indeed, in a prosperous existence such visible forms are easily obtained.”

M04-body-P190.title: Fetters of desire for existence, wrong view and attachment to rules and observances

paragraphs.M04-body-P190-S01: In terms of actual phenomena it is greed clinging to a prosperous existence. In the discourse method, desire for form and desire for the formless can also be given in place of desire for existence. Craving, or greed, that delights in fine-material jhāna and its result is the fetter of desire for form. Craving that delights in immaterial jhāna and its result is the fetter of desire for the formless. Here the commentaries exemplify longing for a prosperous existence replete with all six objects, beginning with visible form. Hence desire for existence can differ in scope from desire for form and for the formless. Understand desire for existence as greed that may be associated with all eight greed-rooted consciousnesses as appropriate.
paragraphs.M04-body-P190-S02: 3. The fetter of wrong view. It arises through holding that same visible object to be (a) permanent, enduring and solid, (b) pleasant and comfortable, or (c) a self, a living entity, a soul, consciousness, or a selfhood. Misapprehending it as permanent, pleasant and self is delusion. Wrongly holding and believing it to be so is wrong view. Each impulsion contains the mentality of the greed-and-wrong-view group, numbering twenty, nineteen, twenty-two, or twenty-one. This is greed associated with wrong view.
paragraphs.M04-body-P190-S03: 4. The fetter of attachment to rules and observances. Thinking that by practising mistaken observances such as the ox or dog practice one can obtain such visible forms in the future, one adheres to such observances…

M04-body-P191.title: Attachment to observances, conceit, aversion and envy

paragraphs.M04-body-P191-S01: … and practises them, the fetter of attachment to rules and observances arises in that continuum. This fetter belongs to the greed-and-wrong-view group of twenty, nineteen, twenty-two or twenty-one mental phenomena, greed associated with wrong view. It is very difficult for that kind of attachment to arise in a worldling who has gone for refuge to the Triple Gem, has confidence in kamma and its results, has right view of ownership of kamma, and is striving for knowledge delimiting mentality and materiality. The explanation here concerns beings in whom that fetter can arise.
paragraphs.M04-body-P191-S02: 5. The fetter of conceit. When one exalts oneself, thinking, “No one apart from me can make the colour of the visible object in these material clusters clear to wisdom. I alone can see it,” the fetter of conceit arises. It is unwholesome impulsion of the greed-and-conceit group, dissociated from wrong view, with twenty, nineteen, twenty-two or twenty-one mental phenomena in each impulsion moment.
paragraphs.M04-body-P191-S03: 6. The fetter of aversion. When one encounters an unwanted, disagreeable visible object and dislikes it or becomes angry, the fetter of aversion arises. This is the mentality of the hatred group. Discern taking a disagreeable visible object as object. Each impulsion contains eighteen or twenty mental phenomena.
paragraphs.M04-body-P191-S04: 7. The fetter of envy. It arises in the continuum of one who envies, thinking, “If only others apart from me could not obtain such visible forms.” This is the mentality of the hatred-and-envy group. In each impulsion…

M04-body-P192.title: Stinginess and remorse over what was done

paragraphs.M04-body-P192-S01: … there are nineteen or twenty-one mental phenomena of the hatred-and-envy group. Discern with the visible form of someone you habitually envy as object. For example, take the colour of another person’s fine, sparkling earrings as object.
paragraphs.M04-body-P192-S02: 8. The fetter of stinginess. In the continuum of one who keeps an acquired visible object to oneself and resents others sharing in it, the fetter of stinginess arises. This is the mentality of the hatred-and-stinginess group, nineteen or twenty-one in each impulsion. Discern taking the colour of an animate or inanimate sensual possession of your own that you habitually cannot bear others to touch. For example, when someone touches your clean garment with an ink-stained hand, you may say nothing but inwardly cannot bear it. Discern taking the object that has stirred or habitually stirs that response.
paragraphs.M04-body-P192-S03: Remorse is not among these ten fetters. Discern two kinds separately: (a) misconduct committed and (b) good conduct omitted. In case (a), remorse arises from later distress over misconduct done in relation to a visible object. This is the hatred-and-remorse group. Discern using the object that previously gave rise to remorse. For example, if you damaged the colour of another’s garment with ink and later felt distressed and unhappy, discern with that same object. In case (b), take a good deed that was omitted…

M04-body-P193.title: Remorse over omission, restlessness, doubt and ignorance

paragraphs.M04-body-P193-S01: … and are later distressed over it, remorse arises. This is the hatred-and-remorse group, with nineteen or twenty-one mental phenomena in each impulsion. For example, if you intended to offer flowers to the Buddha but could not do so and later felt unhappy, discern taking that object. Some meditators find it difficult to discern the hatred-and-remorse group with ultimate reality as object. In that case first apprehend the mentality with a concept as object, then apprehend the same group again with ultimate reality as object.
paragraphs.M04-body-P193-S02: Restlessness does not occur among the ten fetters in the Abhidhamma method given here, but does occur among the ten according to the discourse method. When visible form is taken as object and the mind is agitated, restlessness arises. This is the delusion-and-restlessness group, with sixteen mental phenomena in each impulsion. Greed and hatred are absent. Discern taking as object the colour of a visible form that unsettled the mind.
paragraphs.M04-body-P193-S03: 9. The fetter of doubt. It arises in the continuum of someone who doubts, “Is this visible form a being, a self, something belonging to a being, or something belonging to a self, that is, the colour of a self?” This is the doubt group, with sixteen mental phenomena in each impulsion. Discern with visible form as object, with the doubt whether it is the colour of a self.
paragraphs.M04-body-P193-S04: 10. The fetter of ignorance. Whenever the preceding fetters arise, ignorance, misapprehension, always accompanies them. See Dīgha Commentary, vol. 2, p. 377 and Majjhima Commentary, vol. 1, p. 292. These fetters do not arise in isolation…

M04-body-P194.title: Fetters arise in groups, and the limits of eye-consciousness

paragraphs.M04-body-P194-S01: … but are associated with other consciousness and mental factors and arise in groups. These groups of mentality arise in accordance with the fixed sequence of the cognitive process. When apprehending them, break down the compactness of mentality so that wisdom reaches ultimate reality.
paragraphs.M04-body-P194-S02: A point to note. In explaining the ten fetters arising with visible form, the commentaries say “at the eye-door” (cakkhudvāre), meaning that they can also occur in the eye-door process (Dīgha Commentary, vol. 2, p. 377. Majjhima Commentary, vol. 1, p. 292). When visible form is attended to as permanent, pleasant, self or attractive, many mind-door processes follow the eye-door process. After those mind-door processes have discerned the object in these ways many times, subsequent eye-door processes can bear an imprint of taking the object in those ways. Clear determination as permanent, pleasant, self, or attractive does not occur in the eye-door process itself. Only a general imprint of that nature may be present there. See the commentary and subcommentary below.
paragraphs.M04-body-P194-S03:
Cakkhuviññāṇañhi rūpe rūpamattameva passati, na niccādisabhāvaṃ.
Eye-consciousness sees visible form merely as visible form and does not know characteristics such as permanence or impermanence (Saṃyutta Commentary, vol. 3, p. 28).
paragraphs.M04-body-P194-S04:
Rūpamattamevāti nīlādibhedaṃ rūpāyatanamattaṃ, na nīlādi. Visesanivattanattho hi ayaṃ matta-saddo. Yadi evaṃ, eva-kāro kimatthiyo? Cakkhuviññāṇañhi rūpāyatane labbhamānampi nīlādivisesaṃ “idaṃ nīlaṃ nāma, idaṃ pītaṃ nāmā”ti na gaṇhāti. Kuto niccādisabhāvatthanti…
Subcommentarial passage continued on Burmese page 195.

M04-body-P195.title: Colour in eye-door and mind-door processes

paragraphs.M04-body-P195-S01:
… saṃhitassapi nivattanatthaṃ evakāraggahaṇaṃ. Tenāha “na niccādisabhāvan”ti.
Saṃyutta Subcommentary, vol. 2, p. 303.
paragraphs.M04-body-P195-S02: Subcommentarial passage continued from the preceding page. “Merely visible form” means only the visible-form base, without distinguishing blue and other colours. Colour is still an object of eye-consciousness, but eye-consciousness cannot be said to determine “this is called blue, this is called yellow”. Hence the statement that it does not know characteristics such as permanence or impermanence (Saṃyutta Subcommentary, vol. 2, p. 303).
paragraphs.M04-body-P195-S03: According to the commentary and subcommentary, eye-consciousness, or the group of mental phenomena in the eye-door process with eye-consciousness, knows colour, such as brown and yellow, without distinguishing “brown” or “yellow”. Although it can take visible form as object, it is unable to determine “this is brown, this is yellow”. Still less can it take the actual characteristic as object and determine permanence or impermanence (Saṃyutta Commentary, vol. 3, p. 28. Saṃyutta Subcommentary, vol. 2, p. 303).
paragraphs.M04-body-P195-S04: Nevertheless, wrong view can occur at impulsion in the eye-door process, since all unwholesome impulsions can occur in this process. Therefore, wrong-view-associated consciousness in an eye-door process can bear the imprint of a view held by wrong-view-associated consciousness in mind-door processes, that is, taking the object as permanent, pleasant, self, or attractive. Test this for yourselves. A meditator who has thoroughly discerned materiality before taking up mentality may find it difficult to hold material phenomena to be permanent, pleasant, or self, and may still hold them only as attractive. For one without knowledge of ultimate reality, the views of permanence, pleasure, self, and attractiveness are readily present.

M04-body-P196.title: Eye-door and mind-door process table with unwholesome impulsion

paragraphs.M04-body-P196-S02: Note: For hatred and remorse, discern two cases with misconduct already done as object and two with good conduct omitted as object, four in all.

M04-body-P197.title: How to discern the unwholesome group taking visible form

paragraphs.M04-body-P197-S01: The preceding explanation showed how the ten fetters arise among the consciousness and mental factors of eye-door processes with unwholesome impulsion taking visible form. This is one method of apprehending mentality in eye-door and mind-door processes with unwholesome impulsion and visible form as object. Discern the remaining twenty-seven material phenomena similarly. The greed-and-wrong-view group serves as the example below.
paragraphs.M04-body-P197-S02:
1. If needed, re-establish concentration in stages.
2. Apprehend the two doors together until clear to wisdom: eye-sensitivity, the eye-door, and the clear life-continuum, the mind-door.
3. Direct the mind to the colour of the many material clusters around that eye-sensitivity.
4. When the colour impinges on and appears at both doors together, eye-door and mind-door processes taking that same visible form arise. Five-door adverting, determining and mind-door adverting in these processes attend to the colour as: (a) permanent, enduring, (b) pleasant, comfortable, (c) self, a selfhood, or (d) attractive, beautiful…

M04-body-P198.title: Wrong view at the mind-door and its imprint in the eye-door process

paragraphs.M04-body-P198-S01: … turn to and determine each mode separately. With unwise attention, series of eye-door and mind-door processes with unwholesome impulsion led by greed and wrong view will arise. As explained above, five-door adverting and determining cannot decide conclusively that the object is permanent, pleasant, self, or attractive. Only mind-door adverting in repeatedly arising mind-door processes, or decision associated with it, can decide conclusively. Greed and wrong view in the mind-door processes that decide this way hold the object to be permanent, pleasant, self or attractive. Five-door adverting and determining operate in a manner resembling decision, as already explained.
paragraphs.M04-body-P198-S02: One who sees ultimate reality may find it difficult to discern visible form as permanent, pleasant or self. Holding it to be attractive and becoming infatuated with it, the fetter of sensual desire, can still occur. Holding it to be permanent, pleasant, self, or attractive belongs to the four greed-rooted consciousnesses associated with wrong view. When one delights in an attractive object and the fetter of sensual desire arises, any of the eight greed-rooted consciousnesses can occur as appropriate. The same applies when clinging to visible form and becoming attached to a prosperous existence. Extend the discernment according to your wisdom. With joyful feeling there is joy, and with equanimous feeling there is none. In prompted consciousness there is inducement and sloth and torpor are associated. In unprompted consciousness there is no inducement and they are absent.

M04-body-P199.title: Feeling in investigating, impulsion and registration

paragraphs.M04-body-P199-S01: The table gives the counts of consciousness and mental factors in each process moment. When impulsion has joyful feeling and joy, investigating and registration also have joyful feeling and joy. When impulsion has equanimous feeling without joy, investigating and registration also have equanimous feeling without joy. Investigating and registration generally have the same feeling as impulsion. When impulsion has displeased feeling, however, investigating and registration cannot have displeased feeling, so only equanimous investigating and registration occur.
paragraphs.M04-body-P199-S02: With an exceptionally desirable object only the five joyful registrations can occur. Great-resultant registration with joyful feeling and knowledge (thirty-four mental phenomena), great-resultant registration with joyful feeling but without knowledge (thirty-three), or joyful rootless wholesome-resultant investigating registration (twelve) can occur.
paragraphs.M04-body-P199-S03: With a desirable object the eight kinds of great-resultant registration (thirty-four/thirty-three/thirty-three/thirty-two mental phenomena) and the two kinds of rootless wholesome-resultant registration (twelve/eleven) can occur. With an undesirable object there is only one unwholesome-resultant registration (eleven mental phenomena). The table therefore gives two instances of eleven. One is rootless wholesome-resultant equanimous investigating, the other rootless unwholesome-resultant equanimous investigating. A desirable object gives wholesome result and an undesirable object gives unwholesome result as appropriate. But within a single process…

M04-body-P200.title: Applying the method to sound, odour, taste and tangibles

paragraphs.M04-body-P200-S01: … only one kind of registration can occur. Apprehend the registration that actually occurs.
paragraphs.M04-body-P200-S02: The numbers at five-door adverting, eye-consciousness, receiving, investigating and determining follow the same pattern as the wholesome group. The difference between the wholesome and unwholesome groups is the number of mental phenomena at impulsion. For the other unwholesome groups, such as greed and conceit, hatred and the rest, consult the arising of the ten fetters and discern following the model of greed and wrong view.
paragraphs.M04-body-P200-S03: The groups of sound, odour, taste and tangibles. For visible form, eye-sensitivity and the clear life-continuum were apprehended together, then the colour of desirable or undesirable clusters was taken as object for apprehending the groups with wholesome and with unwholesome impulsion. Follow that model.
paragraphs.M04-body-P200-S04: For sound, apprehend ear-sensitivity together with the clear life-continuum and discern with a desirable or undesirable sound as object. Depending on wise or unwise attention, ear-door and mind-door processes with wholesome or unwholesome impulsion will arise. Similarly, for odour, apprehend nose-sensitivity together with the clear life-continuum and discern taking the desirable or undesirable odour of material clusters as object.

M04-body-P201.title: Taste, tangibles, and the order of the six groups

paragraphs.M04-body-P201-S01: For taste, apprehend tongue-sensitivity together with the clear life-continuum and discern the taste of desirable or undesirable material clusters.
paragraphs.M04-body-P201-S02: For tangibles, apprehend body-sensitivity together with the clear life-continuum and discern the tangibles of desirable or undesirable material clusters. As tangibles comprise the earth, fire and wind elements, apprehend both wholesome and unwholesome groups separately with each element as object. Thus divide tangibles into three and discern three rounds. Apprehension of mentality taking material mind objects was explained above. When you can apprehend the groups with wholesome and unwholesome impulsion in all six domains, proceed in the order visible form, sound, odour, taste, tangibles, and mind objects. This makes it easy to distinguish which groups have been apprehended and which remain.
paragraphs.M04-body-P201-S03: The method presented thus far is the concise method for apprehending jhāna mentality and mentality arising with materiality as object.

M04-body-P202.title: The detailed method of apprehending mentality

paragraphs.M04-body-P202-S01: In the detailed method, apprehend mentality arising with each material phenomenon at the six doors and in the forty-two parts as object. For example, there are fifty-four material phenomena at the eye-door. Begin with mentality taking each of them as object. First, the eye-decad at the eye-door has ten kinds:
paragraphs.M04-body-P202-S02:
1. Earth element — mentality in the tangible-object group.
2. Water element — mind-door mentality in the mind-object group.
3. Fire element — mentality in the tangible-object group.
4. Wind element — mentality in the tangible-object group.
5. Colour, visible form — mentality in the visible-object group.
6. Odour — mentality in the odour group.
7. Taste — mentality in the taste group.
8. Nutriment — mentality in the mind-object group.
9. Life faculty — mentality in the mind-object group.
10. Eye-sensitivity — mentality in the mind-object group.
paragraphs.M04-body-P202-S03: Apprehend each kind of mentality separately in this way. With each material phenomenon as object, apprehend both the processes with wholesome impulsion and those with unwholesome impulsion, both the wholesome and the unwholesome groups. After taking each material phenomenon in the eye-decad as object…

M04-body-P203.title: Applying the detailed method at the six doors and in the forty-two parts

paragraphs.M04-body-P203-S01: … continue with the ten material phenomena in the body-decad, ten in the sex-decad, eight in the consciousness-born cluster, eight in the temperature-born cluster, and eight in the nutriment-born cluster. With each as object, apprehend both wholesome and unwholesome mentality. There are fifty-four rounds at the eye-door. Continue separately with fifty-four at the ear-door, fifty-four at the nose-door, fifty-four at the tongue-door, forty-four at the body-door, and fifty-four at the mind-door in the heart. Also apprehend mentality taking each material phenomenon in the forty-two parts as object. The detailed method can be found in the Visuddhimagga, vol. 2, p. 226. Practise it when needed, if the concise method has yet to succeed.
paragraphs.M04-body-P203-S02: The following summarizes the six groups in meditation on mentality. The mind-object group comprises mind-door mentality taking material mind objects and other ultimate or conceptual phenomena as objects. It is divided into four parts, (a), (b), (c), and (d). When proficient in all six groups, apprehend mentality in the order shown in the following tables.

M04-body-P204.title: Three summary tables of mentality groups

paragraphs.M04-body-P204-S01:
Summary of the six groups

1. Visible form | Wholesome impulsion | Unwholesome impulsion
2. Sound | Wholesome impulsion | Unwholesome impulsion
3. Odour | Wholesome impulsion | Unwholesome impulsion
4. Taste | Wholesome impulsion | Unwholesome impulsion
5. Tangibles | Wholesome impulsion | Unwholesome impulsion
6. Mind objects | Wholesome impulsion | Unwholesome impulsion
(a) Concrete materiality (10/11) | Wholesome impulsion | Unwholesome impulsion
(b) Non-concrete materiality (10) | Wholesome impulsion | Unwholesome impulsion
paragraphs.M04-body-P204-S02:
(c) Mind objects — wholesome mind-door processes
Subject | Mind-door adverting | Impulsion (7) | Rooted registration (2) | Rootless registration (2)
Right speech | 12 | 35/34/34/33 | 34/33/33/32 | 12/11/11
Right action | 12 | 35/34/34/33 | 34/33/33/32 | 12/11/11
Right livelihood | 12 | 35/34/34/33 | 34/33/33/32 | 12/11/11
Compassion | 12 | 35/34/34/33 | × | ×
Appreciative joy | 12 | 35/34/34/33 | × | ×
Recollection of the Buddha | 12 | 34/33/33/32 | 34/33 | 12
Recollection of death | 12 | 34/33/33/32 | 34/33/33/32 | 12/11/11
paragraphs.M04-body-P204-S03:

Subject | Jhānas
Breathing | First, second, third and fourth jhānas
