Space kasiṇa | First, second, third and fourth jhānas
Loving-kindness | First, second and third jhānas
Compassion | First, second and third jhānas
Appreciative joy | First, second and third jhānas
Equanimity | Fourth jhāna
Bones (repulsiveness) | First jhāna
Foulness | First jhāna

M04-body-P205.title: Objects of the four immaterial jhānas and defining mentality

paragraphs.M04-body-P205-S01: If you have attained the immaterial jhānas, apprehend the mind-door together with the corresponding object and then apprehend that jhāna mentality. 1. The object of infinite space is the concept of space without limits. 2. The object of infinite consciousness is the consciousness of infinite space. 3. The object of nothingness is the concept “there is nothing”, the absence of the consciousness of infinite space. 4. The object of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is the consciousness of nothingness.
paragraphs.M04-body-P205-S02: Apprehend the life-continuum mind-door together with the corresponding object, then apprehend the mentality of that jhāna. The pattern is the same as in the fourth-jhāna table. Mind-door adverting has twelve mental phenomena. Preparation, access, conformity and change-of-lineage each have thirty-three. Each absorption impulsion has thirty-one.
paragraphs.M04-body-P205-S03:
So sabbepi te arūpadhamme namanalakkhaṇena ekato katvā taṃ nāmanti passati.
Apprehend mentality as mentality. One brings together all those immaterial phenomena by their characteristic of inclining and sees them as mentality (Visuddhimagga, vol. 2, p. 223).

M04-body-P206.title: Grouping mental phenomena and apprehending mentality and materiality together

paragraphs.M04-body-P206-S01: Following the commentary above, apprehend the mental phenomena as a group. As set out in the tables, when apprehending mentality by doors and bases, begin with knowing consciousness and gradually add contact, feeling, perception, volition and each further mental phenomenon. Once all the phenomena in a moment have been apprehended as in the tables and appear together to wisdom, take their characteristic of inclining towards an object and apprehend them as one group, noting “This is mentality” or “Mentality, mentality”. Wait to apply this collective method until all the co-arising phenomena in each process moment are seen. When seen by wisdom, discern them together.
paragraphs.M04-body-P206-S02:
Rūpārūpānaṃ lakkhaṇādīhi paricchinditvā gahaṇaṃ rūpārūpapariggaho.
Rūpārūpaṃ pana pariggaṇhanto…
Paricchinditvā gahaṇaṃ pariggaho.
Apprehending mentality and materiality together (rūpārūpapariggaha). After delimiting mentality and materiality by characteristics and the other aspects, distinguish them. Mūlaṭīkā, vol. 1, p. 112. Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 1, p. 260. Anuṭīkā, vol. 1, p. 139.

M04-body-P207.title: Base, object and mentality in each moment

paragraphs.M04-body-P207-S01: Following the instruction above, meditators should apprehend and distinguish mentality and materiality by wisdom according to characteristic, function, manifestation and proximate cause. This will be presented separately in the section on characteristics and related aspects. Here the emphasis has been on apprehending ultimate mentality and materiality by their individual characteristics. Since mentality was apprehended by bases and doors, it is appropriate to use that method when apprehending mentality and materiality together. In apprehending supporting materiality as given in the tables, give priority to concrete materiality and also apprehend non-concrete materiality. The tables emphasize concrete materiality that can be an object of insight knowledge. For example, in the eye-door process:
paragraphs.M04-body-P207-S02:
1. At five-door adverting, the fifty-four supporting material phenomena at the heart and the visible object are materiality, and eleven instances of consciousness and mental factors are mentality.
2. At eye-consciousness, the fifty-four supporting material phenomena at the eye and the visible object are materiality, and eight instances of consciousness and mental factors are mentality. Apprehend each process moment fully in this way. Apprehend mentality and materiality together in the same way in all six groups and all rounds. See the tables.

paragraphs.M04-body-P208-S01:
Yopi rūpārūpaṃ pariggahetvā nāmarūpaṃ vavatthapento…
Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 1, p. 260.
paragraphs.M04-body-P208-S02:
Tato namanalakkhaṇaṃ nāmaṃ, ruppanalakkhaṇaṃ rūpanti saṅkhepato nāmarūpaṃ vavatthapeti.
Visuddhimagga, vol. 2, p. 222.
paragraphs.M04-body-P208-S03:
Iti idañca nāmaṃ, idañca rūpaṃ, idaṃ vuccati nāmarūpanti saṅkhepato nāmarūpaṃ vavatthapeti.
Visuddhimagga, vol. 2, p. 223.
paragraphs.M04-body-P208-S04:
Na añño sattādikoti vavatthāpanaṃ nāmarūpavavatthāpanaṃ.
Mūlaṭīkā, vol. 1, p. 112.
paragraphs.M04-body-P208-S05: Once able to apprehend mentality and materiality together in each process moment of all six groups, take that very mentality and materiality as object and see by wisdom that there are only groups of mentality and materiality. There is no person, being, living principle, self, human, deva or brahmā in them. Distinguish thus: “There is no person, being, living principle, self, human, deva or brahmā. There is only mentality and materiality.”

M04-body-P209.title: Part 5. Four kinds of compactness of mentality

paragraphs.M04-body-P209-S01: Compactness (ghana) means a mass or group. Material compactness is a grouping of materiality, and mental compactness a grouping of mentality. The three kinds of material compactness were explained in the section on materiality. The four kinds of mental compactness are presented here.
paragraphs.M04-body-P209-S02:
Santatighanādīnaṃ ayaṃ viseso: purimapacchimānaṃ nirantaratāya ekībhūtānamiva pavatti santatighanatā. Tathā phassādīnaṃ ekasamūhavasena dubbiññeyyakiccabhedavasena ekārammaṇatāvasena ca ekībhūtānamiva pavatti samūhādighanatā.
The subcommentary distinguishes compactness of continuity from compactness of collection. Because of uninterrupted occurrence, the difference between what precedes and what follows is obscured. In such phenomena as contact, lack of analysis into individual constituents makes their collection appear as a compact mass (Mūlaṭīkā, vol. 1, p. 80). When the different elements are analysed, compactness is broken and non-self becomes evident according to its nature (Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 2, p. 47. Visuddhimagga, vol. 2, p. 276).
paragraphs.M04-body-P209-S03:
Nānādhātuyo vinibbhujitvā ghanavinibbhoge kate anattalakkhaṇaṃ yāthāvasarasato upaṭṭhāti.
The subcommentary explains analysis of the different elements as recognizing each by its own nature, such as “the earth element is one phenomenon, the water element another”, or “contact is one phenomenon, feeling another”. In this way wisdom analyses and breaks compactness. The quotation continues on the next page.

M04-body-P210.title: The four kinds of compactness and compactness of continuity

paragraphs.M04-body-P210-S01: The compactness of collection arises when many phenomena co-arising in groups of mentality and materiality appear as one. The compactness of function arises when their distinct functions are undifferentiated. The compactness of object arises when the phenomena taking an object appear as one. When these compact masses are analysed by wisdom, their characteristic of non-self becomes clear, since the phenomena occur according to conditions, empty and ownerless. Thus four kinds of compactness are spoken of (Mahāṭīkā, vol. 2, p. 437).
paragraphs.M04-body-P210-S02: Mentality has four kinds of compactness: 1. Continuity (santatighana). 2. Collection (samūhaghana). 3. Function (kiccaghana). 4. Object (ārammaṇaghana).
paragraphs.M04-body-P210-S03: 1. Compactness of continuity is the apparent connectedness of the mental stream. The eye-door process illustrates the other processes. There is mentality in processes and outside processes. Both occur in groups called mental clusters. Process consciousnesses arise only in the fixed order called the regularity of the cognitive process. When a very great visible object comes before the eye-door and mind-door, the groups of eye-door process mentality arise in sequence as five-door adverting, eye-consciousness, receiving, investigating, determining, seven impulsions and two registrations…

M04-body-P211.title: Breaking compactness of continuity and recognizing compactness of collection

paragraphs.M04-body-P211-S01: … arise without interruption according to the regularity of consciousness (Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 1, p. 128). If wisdom has yet to distinguish each moment of the process, from five-door adverting, eye-consciousness, receiving, investigating, determining, first impulsion … pe … seventh impulsion, to first and second registration, they are grasped as one mass. This is mental compactness of continuity. It is broken when wisdom distinguishes the individual moments. Likewise, for consciousness outside processes, distinguish rebirth-linking, first life-continuum, second life-continuum and subsequent consciousnesses, moment by moment, to break compactness of continuity. Meditators should apprehend mentality in this way.
paragraphs.M04-body-P211-S02: 2. Compactness of collection is the grouping of mentality. Mental phenomena arising according to the regularity of consciousness arise in each moment as a mental cluster. They cannot arise separately. Mental phenomena belonging to a single group are called associated phenomena or a mental cluster. A moment contains at least eight mental phenomena. For example, eye-consciousness and the seven universal mental factors make eight…

paragraphs.M04-body-P212-S01: … there is no mental group smaller than eight. While one has yet to analyse each mental phenomenon in a moment by right view, or wisdom, as “this is contact, this is feeling, this is perception, this is volition, this is consciousness”, and apprehends them as one phenomenon, the compactness of collection has yet to be broken. When each is directly penetrated with wisdom, the compactness of collection is broken. Meditators must analyse with wisdom and apprehend them down to ultimate reality.
paragraphs.M04-body-P212-S02: 3. Compactness of function is the lumping together of the functions of mentality. Even after breaking compactness of continuity and collection, continue to apprehend mentality so as to break compactness of function. Among mental phenomena arising together in each moment: 1. Contact has the function of bringing the object and knowing consciousness together (saṅghaṭṭanarasa). 2. Pleasant feeling has the function of fostering associated phenomena (sampayuttānaṃ upabrūhanarasā). 3. Perception has the function of marking the object so it can be recognized again…

paragraphs.M04-body-P213-S01: … (paccābhiññāṇarasā). 4. Volition has the function of accumulating and constructing (āyūhanarasā). 5. Consciousness has the function of leading in knowing the object (pubbaṅgamarasa).
paragraphs.M04-body-P213-S02: Each mental phenomenon in a moment has its own function. While one has yet to analyse those functions and see them separately with right view, or wisdom, and apprehends them as one function, compactness of function has yet to be broken. When one distinguishes by wisdom, “this is the function of contact, this of feeling, this of perception, this of volition, this of consciousness”, and sees the distinct function of each mental phenomenon in each moment, compactness of function is broken. Meditators need to analyse and apprehend mentality by right view in this way.
paragraphs.M04-body-P213-S03: Mentality in an eye-door process takes visible form alone and can arise only with that visible form as object. It therefore consists of phenomena having an object (sārammaṇa). The three kinds of compactness of continuity, collection and function have been explained for that object-taking eye-door mentality.

M04-body-P214.title: Compactness of object and the two sides of insight

paragraphs.M04-body-P214-S01: Another group of mentality exhibits compactness of object (ārammaṇaghana), the compactness of mental phenomena taking an object. Insight involves two kinds: mentality discerned as object and mentality led by insight knowledge that discerns that object. The discerning mentality also has an object. The compactness of continuity, collection and function must be broken in the mentality discerned, and likewise in the insight mentality doing the discerning. The section on comprehension by groups (Visuddhimagga, vol. 2, pp. 260–262) and the higher knowledges such as dissolution give the following instruction:
paragraphs.M04-body-P214-S02:
Ñātañca ñāṇañca ubhopi vipassati.
One discerns with insight both what is known and the knowledge (Visuddhimagga, vol. 2, p. 278).
paragraphs.M04-body-P214-S03: 1. What is known (ñāta) is the five aggregates subject to clinging belonging to the truth of suffering and formations such as ignorance, craving, clinging and kamma belonging to the truth of origin, which insight knowledge must penetrate. 2. Knowledge (ñāṇa) is the mentality led by the insight knowledge doing the discerning. Discern both by the three characteristics. The mental group led by the discerning insight knowledge…

M04-body-P215.title: Three kinds of compactness in the insight process

paragraphs.M04-body-P215-S01: … in worldlings and trainees consists of mind-door process series with great wholesome impulsion. Mind-door adverting has twelve mental phenomena, and each of seven impulsion moments has thirty-four, thirty-three, thirty-three or thirty-two as appropriate. With weak insight there can be registration. With strong insight such as knowledge of dissolution, registration has no opportunity to occur. Sometimes thirty-three is shown because wisdom can be associated. Sometimes joy is absent, so thirty-three or thirty-two is also shown.
paragraphs.M04-body-P215-S02: For a mind-door process series with impulsion led by discerning insight knowledge: 1. Distinguish each moment as mind-door adverting, first impulsion, second impulsion, and so forth, to break compactness of continuity. 2. Distinguish “this is contact, feeling, perception, volition, consciousness” and so forth in each moment to break compactness of collection. 3. Use wisdom to distinguish the separate function of each mental phenomenon in each moment to break compactness of function.
paragraphs.M04-body-P215-S03: Thus there are three kinds of compactness on the side of mentality discerned and three on the side led by discerning wisdom. Those in the mentality discerned are separately called compactness of continuity, collection and function. The three on the side of discerning wisdom are collectively called compactness of object…

M04-body-P216.title: Breaking compactness of object to see non-self

paragraphs.M04-body-P216-S01: … When the phenomena taking an object remain undifferentiated and are grasped as one, compactness of object persists. When one distinguishes each moment from mind-door adverting to the first impulsion … pe … the seventh, and distinguishes contact, feeling, perception, volition, consciousness and their respective functions, compactness of object is broken.
paragraphs.M04-body-P216-S02: The meditator must break the compactness of mentality and materiality by wisdom, apprehend and distinguish them, and discern them with insight to penetrate ultimate reality. Penetrating ultimate reality makes it possible to see non-self, and penetrating non-self makes it possible to reach path knowledge, fruition knowledge, and Nibbāna. The commentaries say:
paragraphs.M04-body-P216-S03:
Nānādhātuyo vinibbhujitvā ghanavinibbhoge kate anattalakkhaṇaṃ yāthāvasarasato upaṭṭhāti.
When the different elements are analysed and compactness is broken, the characteristic of non-self appears according to its actual nature (Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 2, p. 47. Visuddhimagga, vol. 2, p. 276).

M04-body-P217.title: The characteristic of non-self and three insights

paragraphs.M04-body-P217-S01: Thus the characteristic of non-self, the true nature of the phenomena, becomes clear in the meditator’s wisdom (Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 2, p. 47. Visuddhimagga, vol. 2, p. 276).
paragraphs.M04-body-P217-S02: Discern the formations called what is known (ñāta) and knowledge (ñāṇa) by the three characteristics. When insight into impermanence, suffering and non-self matures, the noble path can be reached (Visuddhimagga, vol. 2, p. 301). Since compactness must be broken for wisdom to penetrate non-self, proceed to apprehend formations of mentality and materiality by characteristic, function, manifestation and proximate cause. This will become clear in the section on those four aspects.

paragraphs.M04-body-P218-S01:
1. Once able to discern the four elements, discern them while walking, standing, sitting and lying down, and in activities of clear comprehension such as stepping forward, stepping back, looking straight ahead, looking aside, bending and stretching.
2. Once able to discern materiality, discern all material phenomena in those postures and activities (rūpapariggaha).
3. Once able to apprehend mentality, discern it in those postures and activities (arūpapariggaha).
4. Once able to apprehend mentality and materiality together, apprehend and distinguish them in those postures and activities (rūpārūpapariggaha).
5. Once able to delimit mentality and materiality…

M04-body-P219.title: Discerning the five aggregates in postures and activities

paragraphs.M04-body-P219-S01: … delimit mentality and materiality also in the activities of clear comprehension (nāmarūpavavatthāna). Apprehending in this way brings one within the scope of discerning the five aggregates. Materiality is the materiality aggregate. Mentality in each moment falls into four mental aggregates: feeling, perception, formations and consciousness. Apart from feeling and perception, all mental factors in a moment belong to the formations aggregate. One material and four mental aggregates make five. An aggregate means a group.
paragraphs.M04-body-P219-S02: Discern the five aggregates: 1. While walking. 2. While standing. 3. While sitting. 4. While lying down. 5. When stepping forward. 6. When stepping back. 7. When looking straight ahead (eye-door and mind-door processes). 8. When looking aside (eye-door and mind-door processes). 9. When bending the limbs. 10. When stretching the limbs. 11. When carrying the double robe. 12. When carrying the bowl. 13. When carrying the robe. 14. When eating. 15. When drinking…

M04-body-P220.title: An example of discerning the five aggregates while looking

paragraphs.M04-body-P220-S01: 16. When licking. 17. When chewing. 18. When defecating. 19. When urinating. 20. While walking. 21. While standing. 22. While sitting. 23. While sleeping. 24. When waking up. 25. When speaking. 26. When silent. Understand how to discern the five aggregates in these cases (see Majjhima Commentary, vol. 1, pp. 255–257).
paragraphs.M04-body-P220-S02:
Ettha hi cakkhu ceva rūpañca rūpakkhandho, dassanaṃ viññāṇakkhandho, taṃsampayuttā vedanā vedanākkhandho, saññā saññākkhandho, phassādikā saṅkhārakkhandho. Evam etesaṃ pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ samavāye ālokanavilokanaṃ paññāyati.
The commentary explains that the eye and visible form belong to the materiality aggregate, seeing consciousness to the consciousness aggregate, associated feeling to the feeling aggregate, perception to the perception aggregate, and contact and similar phenomena to the formations aggregate. Looking straight ahead and looking aside are apparent through the conjunction of these five aggregates (Majjhima Commentary, vol. 1, pp. 267–268).
paragraphs.M04-body-P220-S03: When looking straight ahead or aside, groups of eye-door and mind-door mentality have arisen. At the moment of eye-consciousness the five aggregates are as follows. 1. Eye-sensitivity and visible form, that is, the fifty-four material phenomena at the eye and the visible object, belong to the materiality aggregate…

M04-body-P221.title: The five aggregates in the eye-door process and the walking exercise

paragraphs.M04-body-P221-S01: 2. Eye-consciousness that sees visible form is the consciousness aggregate. 3. Its associated feeling is the feeling aggregate. 4. Perception is the perception aggregate. 5. Contact, volition, one-pointedness, life faculty and attention are the formations aggregate. When these five aggregates combine, looking straight ahead or aside becomes apparent (Majjhima Commentary, vol. 1, pp. 267–268).
paragraphs.M04-body-P221-S02: Eye-consciousness cannot arise without preceding five-door adverting. When it occurs, a slight-object process can reach determining, a great-object process impulsion, and a very-great-object process registration. Thus, once able to discern the five aggregates at eye-consciousness, apprehend them at every remaining moment beginning with five-door adverting. The commentary indicates this through characteristic, indication and example.
paragraphs.M04-body-P221-S03: Exercise. Stand at one end of the walking path and re-establish concentration in stages. Apprehend materiality at the six doors and in the forty-two parts, then take a few steps. Of the material phenomena that bring about motion and those moved, either group can be given priority…

paragraphs.M04-body-P222-S01: … in apprehending each material phenomenon. Distinguish predominant (padhāna) and non-predominant materiality (appadhāna).
paragraphs.M04-body-P222-S02: 1. Predominant materiality. Among consciousness-born clusters, with the non-concrete materiality included, are the ninefold cluster with bodily intimation and the twelvefold cluster with bodily intimation, lightness, malleability, wieldiness and the accompanying phenomena. The nine or twelve material phenomena in these two kinds of cluster are predominant when discerning postures and activities of clear comprehension. The wind element is especially strong in them. That strong wind element gives rise to bodily intimation, the bodily action.
paragraphs.M04-body-P222-S03: 2. Non-predominant materiality. The remaining material phenomena throughout the body at the six doors and in the forty-two parts are non-predominant. “Non-predominant” here refers specifically to discernment of postures and clear comprehension.

M04-body-P223.title: Materiality producing motion and materiality moved

paragraphs.M04-body-P223-S01: Predominant materiality causes the remaining bodily clusters originated by kamma, consciousness, temperature and nutriment to occur in the manner of walking. The postural materiality producing motion, the ninefold or twelvefold clusters with bodily intimation, does not literally carry materiality from one place to another. “Producing motion” means causing materiality to arise successively at new locations. Ultimate materiality cannot leave the place of its arising and ceases there. As conditions continue to operate, new materiality arises in succession at new locations. This continuity is due to the strength of the clusters with strong wind element and bodily intimation.
paragraphs.M04-body-P223-S02: Non-predominant materiality, the remaining phenomena produced by the four origins at the six doors and in the forty-two parts, is the materiality moved. These phenomena are not literally carried away…

M04-body-P224.title: The simile of a person carrying a sack of rice

paragraphs.M04-body-P224-S01: … “being moved” means arising continuously at new locations in succession. When one apprehends the materiality producing motion as primary, apprehending the non-predominant materiality moved is accomplished along with it. That is, when attention is given to the materiality producing motion, the materiality moved is easily seen and discerned.
paragraphs.M04-body-P224-S02: One may also give priority to the materiality moved, produced by the four origins. Giving priority to the non-predominant materiality moved makes it possible to see the predominant materiality producing motion. When the materiality moved is discerned as primary, discernment of the materiality producing motion is accomplished along with it (see Majjhima Commentary, vol. 1, p. 273).
paragraphs.M04-body-P224-S03: For example, when someone carries a sack of rice, attending to the carrier makes the sack easy to see. Attending to the sack likewise makes the carrier easy to see. Remember this simile. See the section on materiality.

M04-body-P225.title: How to discern the five aggregates while walking

paragraphs.M04-body-P225-S01: As explained above, stand on the walking path and re-establish your highest attained concentration. Analyse and apprehend the materiality from the four origins at the six doors and in the forty-two parts. Then step forward a little. Apprehend by giving priority in turn to the materiality producing motion and to that moved. Both belong to the materiality aggregate.
paragraphs.M04-body-P225-S02: The mind-door process series with impulsion wishing to walk directly produce the postural materiality that brings about motion, and belong to the four mental aggregates. Apprehend those four aggregates. In these mind-door series, impulsion can be wholesome, functional or unwholesome. Mind-door processes are specified because five-door impulsion processes cannot produce postural materiality. Each mind-door process moment has four mental aggregates: feeling is the feeling aggregate, perception the perception aggregate, the remaining factors the formations aggregate, and knowing consciousness the consciousness aggregate. Supporting materiality, the postural materiality producing motion, and the materiality moved are the materiality aggregate. Together there are five aggregates. Once able to apprehend the five, apprehend mentality and materiality together, then distinguish them. Do the same in postures and activities of clear comprehension…

M04-body-P226.title: Four tasks and internal and external contemplation

paragraphs.M04-body-P226-S01: … continue the four tasks: 1. Apprehending materiality (rūpapariggaha). 2. Apprehending mentality (arūpapariggaha). 3. Apprehending mentality and materiality together (rūpārūpapariggaha). 4. Delimiting mentality and materiality (nāmarūpavavatthāna). Once able to practise in this way, proceed a further step as the Buddha taught in the Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna Sutta.
paragraphs.M04-body-P226-S02:
Iti ajjhattaṃ vā kāye kāyānupassī viharati, bahiddhā vā kāye kāyānupassī viharati, ajjhattabahiddhā vā kāye kāyānupassī viharati.
One dwells contemplating body as body internally, externally, or both internally and externally (Majjhima Nikāya, vol. 1, p. 73).
paragraphs.M04-body-P226-S03:
Iti ajjhattaṃ vā vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati, bahiddhā vā vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati, ajjhattabahiddhā vā vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati.
One dwells contemplating feelings as feelings internally, externally, or both internally and externally (Majjhima Nikāya, vol. 1, p. 75…).
paragraphs.M04-body-P226-S04:
Iti ajjhattaṃ vā citte cittānupassī viharati, bahiddhā vā citte cittānupassī viharati, ajjhattabahiddhā vā citte cittānupassī viharati.
One dwells contemplating mind as mind internally, externally, or both internally and externally (Majjhima Nikāya, vol. 1, p. 76).
paragraphs.M04-body-P226-S05:
Iti ajjhattaṃ vā dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati, bahiddhā vā dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati, ajjhattabahiddhā vā dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati.
One dwells contemplating phenomena as phenomena internally, externally, or both internally and externally (Majjhima Nikāya, vol. 1, p. 77).
paragraphs.M04-body-P226-S06: In the foregoing Pāli, body, feelings, mind and phenomena refer to the five aggregates, that is, mentality and materiality…

M04-body-P227.title: Why both internal and external contemplation are needed

paragraphs.M04-body-P227-S01: … Repeatedly apprehend and discern the five aggregates internally, externally, and both internally and externally. This is the Buddha’s instruction. The commentaries explain how to proceed in accordance with it.
paragraphs.M04-body-P227-S02:
Yasmā pana na suddhaajjhattadassanamatteneva maggavuṭṭhānaṃ hoti, bahiddhāpi daṭṭhabbameva. Tasmā parassa khandhepi anupādinnasaṅkhārepi aniccaṃ dukkhamanattāti passati.
Seeing only internally cannot bring emergence into the path. The external must also be seen. Hence one sees the aggregates of others and non-clung-to formations as impermanent, suffering, and non-self (Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 1, p. 270. Visuddhimagga, vol. 2, p. 300).
paragraphs.M04-body-P227-S03: Insight leading to emergence (vuṭṭhānagāminivipassanā) comprises two or three mind-door processes with insight impulsion immediately preceding the path process, emerging from formations as object towards Nibbāna, the unconditioned, the stilling of formations.

M04-body-P228.title: The external domain and how to begin

paragraphs.M04-body-P228-S01:
Tasmā sasantānagate sabbadhamme, parasantānagate ca tesaṃ santānavibhāgaṃ akatvā bahiddhābhāvasāmaññato sammasanaṃ, ayaṃ sāvakānaṃ sammasanacāro.
The disciples’ scope of comprehension is to discern all phenomena in their own continuum and the phenomena in others’ continua under the common designation external, without separating those continua (Majjhima Subcommentary, Uparipaṇṇāsa, subcommentary to the Anupada Sutta).
paragraphs.M04-body-P228-S02: According to this instruction, when discerning externally within the scope of a disciple’s wisdom, do not separate males, females, persons, beings, humans, devas, brahmās or particular individuals. Discern collectively the five aggregates of living beings and temperature-born materiality in inanimate things, called non-clung-to formations. There is no need to discern each individual separately.
paragraphs.M04-body-P228-S03: Once able to apprehend the internal five aggregates, mentality and materiality, down to ultimate reality, one can begin apprehending the external five aggregates. Some meditators begin externally. Those beginning internally still need to apprehend external aggregates and non-clung-to formations, since internal discernment alone cannot reach the noble path. Similarly, those who begin externally…

M04-body-P229.title: Apprehending external materiality from clothing to inanimate objects

paragraphs.M04-body-P229-S01: … must also apprehend the internal five aggregates, since external discernment alone cannot reach the noble path (see Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 1, pp. 270–271. Visuddhimagga, vol. 2, p. 300).
paragraphs.M04-body-P229-S02: 1. Re-establish concentration if needed. 2. When the light is strong, apprehend internal materiality again. 3. With the aid of that light, apprehend the four elements in the clothing being worn.
paragraphs.M04-body-P229-S03: Seeing the four elements in clothing with wisdom makes the minute material clusters easy to see. If unsuccessful, return to internal materiality and then to the four elements in the clothing. When the mass of the elements is seen, attend to the space element with the aid of the light. The minute clusters will readily appear. The clothing will then appear as a collection of clusters. Analyse them. The materiality in each is temperature-born materiality with nutriment as the eighth, arising in succession due to the fire element in the cluster. Gradually extend wisdom to the four elements in trees, water, earth, forests, mountains, gold, silver, bricks and stones…

M04-body-P230.title: Extending external discernment of materiality and mentality

paragraphs.M04-body-P230-S01: … in the inanimate world. When only the minute clusters are seen, analyse them until wisdom penetrates ultimate materiality. There are only two kinds in the inanimate world: temperature-born octads and temperature-born octads with sound.
paragraphs.M04-body-P230-S02: Continue apprehending concrete and non-concrete materiality at the six doors and in the forty-two parts of the external animate world following the internal pattern. Begin nearby. For example, apprehend the fifty-four material phenomena at the eye internally, then the fifty-four at nearby external eyes collectively, without distinguishing males, females, brahmās or particular individuals. Apprehend one round internally and one externally to strengthen development. Do likewise at the remaining five doors and in the forty-two parts. When all concrete and non-concrete materiality there is seen, apprehend it as “materiality, materiality”, alternating internal and external. Gradually extend to the thirty-one planes and, if possible, to innumerable world systems. Remember that alternating internal and external strengthens development.
paragraphs.M04-body-P230-S03: Next apprehend mentality in all six groups following the internal pattern. For example, when apprehending visible-object mentality internally, apprehend the eye-door and mind-door together and take as object the colour of many material clusters or of one cluster. According to wise attention…

paragraphs.M04-body-P231-S01: … or unwise attention, apprehend the wholesome or unwholesome group in eye-door and mind-door processes. Follow the same pattern externally, collectively, without separating eye-sensitivity, life-continuum and visible form by individual.
paragraphs.M04-body-P231-S02: 1. Apprehend simultaneously eye-sensitivity, the eye-door, and the clear life-continuum, the mind-door. 2. Take the colour of many material clusters or of one cluster as object. Apprehend wholesome and unwholesome mentality of eye-door and mind-door processes arising according to wise or unwise attention. Understand the sound group and the remaining groups similarly. If discernment can reach as far as the thirty-one planes, gradually extend it to innumerable world systems. Alternate internal and external to strengthen development.
paragraphs.M04-body-P231-S03: When discerning external mentality and materiality, group them by the shared feature of being external, without separating continua by male, female, person, being, human, deva, brahmā or individual. In discerning the thirty-two parts externally, the thirty-two parts in a being’s continuum can be discerned…

M04-body-P232.title: The scope of insight and four steps of practice

paragraphs.M04-body-P232-S01: … Thus in apprehending external materiality, one can analyse and discern all materiality, including that in the thirty-two parts of a being’s continuum. As for mentality, within the scope of insight one cannot know precisely another individual’s mind by insight knowledge. Knowing another person’s mind precisely belongs to the direct knowledge of others’ minds (cetopariyañāṇa). In insight, discern collectively without separating persons and beings. This is the disciples’ domain of comprehension, the scope of knowledge discerning by the three characteristics.
paragraphs.M04-body-P232-S02: When successful in apprehending mentality and materiality both internally and externally, practise in sequence in both domains: 1. Apprehend materiality separately at the six doors and in the forty-two parts. 2. Apprehend mentality separately in all six groups. 3. Apprehend and distinguish mentality and materiality together in all six groups. 4. Delimit mentality and materiality in all six groups.
paragraphs.M04-body-P232-S03: After repeatedly performing those four tasks internally and externally, proceed a step further as instructed by the Buddha below…

M04-body-P233.title: Contemplating arising and passing away by condition and by moment

paragraphs.M04-body-P233-S01:
Samudayadhammānupassī vā kāyasmiṃ viharati, vayadhammānupassī vā kāyasmiṃ viharati, samudayavayadhammānupassī vā kāyasmiṃ viharati.
One dwells contemplating the nature of arising in the body, the nature of passing away in the body, or both (Majjhima Nikāya, vol. 1, p. 73). The same pattern is taught for feelings, mind and phenomena.
paragraphs.M04-body-P233-S02: Here the Buddha teaches developing insight up to seeing arising and passing away by condition (paccayato udayabbayadassana) and by moment (khaṇato udayabbayadassana).
paragraphs.M04-body-P233-S03:
1. See the arising of the five resultant aggregates because such causes as ignorance, craving, clinging, formations and kamma arise. This is seeing arising by condition.
2. See that the five resultant aggregates do not arise again after final Nibbāna because causes such as ignorance, craving, clinging, formations and kamma have been cut off by the arahant path and do not arise again. This is seeing passing away by condition.
3. See the moment of arising of both causes and effects, seeing arising by moment.
4. See the moment of dissolution of both causes and effects…

M04-body-P234.title: Three knowledges and two ways of apprehending conditions

paragraphs.M04-body-P234-S01: … seeing passing away by moment. The Buddha taught apprehending these four aspects by wisdom and discerning the causative and resultant formations according to the three characteristics. Here he teaches together knowledge apprehending conditions, comprehension knowledge, and knowledge of arising and passing away. Knowledge apprehending conditions also has two modes: apprehending conditions and apprehending by inference.
paragraphs.M04-body-P234-S02: Apprehending conditions (paccayapariggaha) emphasizes seeing the five present effects, consciousness, mentality-materiality, the six bases, contact and feeling, arising because of the respective past causes cultivated, such as ignorance, craving, clinging, formations and kamma. Apprehending by inference (anvayapariggaha) apprehends the corresponding causes and effects in successive past and future lives. Both are collectively called knowledge apprehending conditions, also the section on purification by overcoming doubt. Development of this knowledge will be explained in the section on dependent origination by the fifth and first methods.

M04-body-P235.title: Developing the four foundations of mindfulness and choosing a starting point

paragraphs.M04-body-P235-S01:
Yasmā pana na suddharūpadassanamatteneva vuṭṭhānaṃ hoti, arūpampi daṭṭhabbameva.
Insight into materiality alone by the three characteristics cannot reach noble path knowledge or amount to insight leading to emergence. Mentality too must be discerned by the three characteristics (Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 1, p. 270. Visuddhimagga, vol. 2, p. 300).
paragraphs.M04-body-P235-S02: When first attending to and apprehending mentality and materiality as objects of insight, one may begin with either materiality or mentality. Beginning with materiality is possible both for one whose vehicle is tranquillity and for one whose vehicle is insight (see Visuddhimagga, vol. 2, p. 222. Mahāṭīkā, vol. 2, p. 373).
paragraphs.M04-body-P235-S03:
Pariggahite rūpakammaṭṭhāneti idaṃ rūpamukhena vipassanābhinivesaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, arūpamukhena pana vipassanābhiniveso yebhuyyena samathayānikassa icchitabbo. So ca paṭhamaṃ jhānaṅgāni pariggahetvā tato paraṃ sesadhamme pariggaṇhāti.
The subcommentary says that “having apprehended materiality” implies beginning insight with materiality. Starting from mentality is more usual for one whose vehicle is tranquillity, who first apprehends the jhāna factors and then the associated phenomena (Majjhima Subcommentary, vol. 1, p. 369). The bare-insight practitioner generally begins apprehending mentality and materiality as insight objects with materiality…

M04-body-P236.title: Beginning with materiality or mentality and proceeding with both

paragraphs.M04-body-P236-S01: … For this reason the commentary says that one wishing to begin the subject of mentality should first have apprehended materiality. Beginning with mentality in apprehending the objects of insight is generally appropriate for one whose vehicle is tranquillity. Such a person first apprehends the jhāna factors, then the associated phenomena together with mentality and materiality called ordinary formations (Majjhima Subcommentary, vol. 1, p. 369). See also Visuddhimagga, vol. 2, p. 222, and Mahāṭīkā, vol. 2, p. 373.
paragraphs.M04-body-P236-S02: Even when beginning with materiality as an insight object, discerning materiality alone cannot reach the noble path. Continue to apprehend and discern mentality arising with materiality as object. Even when beginning with mental formations as insight objects, discerning mentality alone cannot reach the noble path. Continue to apprehend and discern materiality. Earlier the Aparijānana Sutta was cited, where the Buddha says suffering cannot be ended without fully distinguishing and knowing all five aggregates of mentality and materiality through the three kinds of full understanding…

M04-body-P237.title: The four foundations distinguished in the preparatory phase

paragraphs.M04-body-P237-S01: The Buddha teaches that suffering cannot be ended without fully distinguishing and knowing all five aggregates through the three kinds of full understanding. The commentaries also explain that neither discerning materiality alone nor mentality alone can reach the noble path. When discerning materiality, distinguish the elements and derived materiality by wisdom and discern them with insight. When discerning mentality, distinguish by wisdom the four mental aggregates of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness arising with materiality as object and discern them with insight (Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 1, pp. 270–271. Visuddhimagga, vol. 2, pp. 300–301). The discourses and commentaries agree like the waters of the Gaṅgā and Yamunā. Thus the commentaries explain the foundations of mindfulness as follows.
paragraphs.M04-body-P237-S02:
Iti ime cattāro satipaṭṭhānā pubbabhāge nānācittesu labbhanti. Aññeneva hi cittena kāyaṃ pariggaṇhāti, aññena vedanaṃ, aññena cittaṃ, aññena dhamme pariggaṇhāti. Lokuttaramaggakkhaṇe pana ekacitteyeva labbhanti. Ādito hi kāyaṃ pariggaṇhitvā āgatassa vipassanāsampayuttā sati kāyānupassanā nāma, tāya satiyā samannāgato puggalo kāyānupassī nāma. Vipassanaṃ ussukkāpetvā ariyamaggaṃ pattassa maggakkhaṇe maggasampayuttā sati kāyānupassanā nāma, tāya satiyā samannāgato puggalo kāyānupassī nāma. Vedanaṃ pariggaṇhitvā, cittaṃ pariggaṇhitvā, dhamme pariggaṇhitvā āgatassa vipassanāsampayuttā sati…
Question: Are the four foundations of mindfulness obtained in different consciousnesses in the preparatory phase? Yes. One apprehends body, feelings, mind and phenomena in different consciousnesses. At the supramundane moment, however, they are obtained in the same consciousness. After apprehending the body, mindfulness associated with insight is called contemplation of the body, and one endowed with it a contemplator of the body. When insight is brought to maturity and the noble path is reached, mindfulness associated with the path is likewise called contemplation of the body, and one endowed with it a contemplator of the body. Similarly, after apprehending feelings, mind, or phenomena…

M04-body-P238.title: Four functions of one mindfulness at the path moment

paragraphs.M04-body-P238-S01:
… dhammānupassanā nāma, tāya satiyā samannāgato puggalo dhammānupassī nāma. Vipassanaṃ ussukkāpetvā ariyamaggaṃ pattassa maggakkhaṇe maggasampayuttā sati dhammānupassanā nāma, tāya satiyā samannāgato puggalo dhammānupassī nāma. Evaṃ tāva desanā puggale tiṭṭhati.
… mindfulness associated with insight and mindfulness associated with the noble path are respectively called contemplation of feelings, mind or phenomena. A person endowed with the relevant mindfulness is called a contemplator of feelings, mind or phenomena. This is exposition in terms of the person.
paragraphs.M04-body-P238-S02:
Kāye pana “subhan”ti vipallāsappahānā kāyapariggāhikā sati maggena samijjhatīti kāyānupassanā nāma. Vedanāya “sukhan”ti vipallāsappahānā vedanāpariggāhikā sati maggena samijjhatīti vedanānupassanā nāma. Citte “niccan”ti vipallāsappahānā cittapariggāhikā sati maggena samijjhatīti cittānupassanā nāma. Dhammesu “attā”ti vipallāsappahānā dhammapariggāhikā sati maggena samijjhatīti dhammānupassanā nāma.
In terms of phenomena, 1. Mindfulness apprehending the body, abandoning the distortion of seeing beauty in it, is fulfilled by the path and is called contemplation of the body. 2. Mindfulness apprehending feeling, abandoning the distortion of seeing pleasure in it, is fulfilled by the path and is called contemplation of feelings. 3. Mindfulness apprehending mind, abandoning the distortion of seeing permanence in it, is fulfilled by the path and is called contemplation of mind. 4. Mindfulness apprehending phenomena, abandoning the distortion of seeing self in them, is fulfilled by the path and is called contemplation of phenomena.
paragraphs.M04-body-P238-S03:
Iti ekāva maggasampayuttā sati catukiccasādhanena cattāri nāmāni labhati. Tena vuttaṃ “lokuttaramaggakkhaṇe pana ekacitteyeva labbhantī”ti.
Question: Why does one mindfulness associated with the path have four names? Because it accomplishes four functions. Hence the four foundations are said to be obtained in a single consciousness at the supramundane moment (Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 2, pp. 273–274).
paragraphs.M04-body-P238-S04: The Buddha teaches contemplation of the body with both tranquillity and insight. Contemplation of feelings, mind and phenomena is taught by insight. Before the noble path, the four foundations are obtained in different consciousnesses: 1. Consciousness apprehending the body is one distinct kind. 2. Consciousness apprehending feelings is a distinct kind…

M04-body-P239.title: Contemplation of body and feelings, and names according to the person

paragraphs.M04-body-P239-S01: … 3. Consciousness apprehending mind is a distinct kind. 4. Consciousness apprehending phenomena is a distinct kind. At the supramundane noble-path moment, however, all four foundations are obtained in a single consciousness.
paragraphs.M04-body-P239-S02: 1. When a meditator initially apprehends and distinguishes the body by wisdom and proceeds to insight, mindfulness associated with that insight knowledge is called contemplation of the body (kāyānupassanā). A person endowed with it is a contemplator of the body (kāyānupassī). When the meditator strives to bring insight to the noble path, mindfulness associated with the path is also called contemplation of the body, and one endowed with it a contemplator of the body. There are two bodies, the mental body and the material body (Paṭisambhidāmagga, vol. 1, pp. 177–178).
paragraphs.M04-body-P239-S03:
2. When a meditator initially apprehends and distinguishes feelings by wisdom and proceeds to insight, mindfulness associated with that insight knowledge is called contemplation of feelings (vedanānupassanā). One endowed with it is a contemplator of feelings (vedanānupassī). When the meditator strives to bring insight to the noble path, mindfulness associated with the path is also called contemplation of feelings, and one endowed with it a contemplator of feelings.
3. When a meditator initially apprehends and distinguishes mind by wisdom and proceeds to insight…

M04-body-P240.title: Contemplation of mind and phenomena, and names according to phenomena

paragraphs.M04-body-P240-S01: … mindfulness associated with insight knowledge is called contemplation of mind (cittānupassanā). One endowed with it is a contemplator of mind (cittānupassī). When the meditator strives to bring insight to the noble path, mindfulness associated with the path is likewise called contemplation of mind, and one endowed with it a contemplator of mind.
paragraphs.M04-body-P240-S02: 4. When a meditator initially apprehends and distinguishes phenomena by wisdom and proceeds to insight, mindfulness associated with insight knowledge is called contemplation of phenomena (dhammānupassanā). One endowed with it is a contemplator of phenomena (dhammānupassī). When the meditator strives to bring insight to the noble path, mindfulness associated with the path is likewise called contemplation of phenomena, and one endowed with it a contemplator of phenomena.
paragraphs.M04-body-P240-S03: The names contemplator of body, feelings, mind and phenomena follow the course of insight before reaching the noble path. This is exposition by person. For exposition by phenomena understand as follows. 1. Mindfulness apprehends and distinguishes the body, abandons the distortion that grasps it as beautiful, and is fulfilled through the noble path. Thus it is called contemplation of the body. 2. Mindfulness apprehends and distinguishes feelings and abandons the distortion that grasps them as pleasant…

paragraphs.M04-body-P241-S01: … and is fulfilled through the noble path, so it is called contemplation of feelings. 3. Mindfulness apprehends and distinguishes mind, abandons the distortion that grasps it as permanent, and is fulfilled through the noble path, so it is called contemplation of mind. 4. Mindfulness apprehends and distinguishes phenomena, abandons the distortion that grasps them as self, and is fulfilled through the noble path, so it is called contemplation of phenomena.
paragraphs.M04-body-P241-S02: One mindfulness associated with the noble path has four names because it completes the four tasks of abandoning distortions that grasp beauty, pleasure, permanence and self. Thus the commentary says that the four foundations are obtained in one consciousness at the supramundane noble-path moment (Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 2, pp. 273–274).
paragraphs.M04-body-P241-S03: The discourse states that without fully distinguishing the mentality and materiality of the five aggregates subject to clinging by the three kinds of full understanding, one cannot reach the noble path or put an end to the suffering of saṃsāra. The commentaries also say that discerning the internal five aggregates alone, the external alone, materiality alone, or mentality alone cannot lead to the noble path…

M04-body-P242.title: Practising the four foundations from four starting points

paragraphs.M04-body-P242-S01: … In light of these instructions, remember the four foundations as follows.
paragraphs.M04-body-P242-S02: Begin with materiality, apprehend mentality and materiality, and seek their conditions. Discerning that mentality and materiality with their conditions according to the three characteristics is developing the foundation of mindfulness called contemplation of the body.
paragraphs.M04-body-P242-S03: Begin with feeling, apprehend mentality and materiality, and seek their conditions. Discerning that mentality and materiality with their conditions according to the three characteristics is developing the foundation of mindfulness called contemplation of feelings.
paragraphs.M04-body-P242-S04: Begin with knowing consciousness, apprehend mentality and materiality, and seek their conditions. Discerning that mentality and materiality with their conditions according to the three characteristics is developing the foundation of mindfulness called contemplation of mind.
paragraphs.M04-body-P242-S05: Begin with contact, apprehend mentality and materiality, and seek their conditions. Discerning that mentality and materiality with their conditions according to the three characteristics is developing the foundation of mindfulness called contemplation of phenomena.
paragraphs.M04-body-P242-S06: For contemplation of phenomena one may also begin with the five hindrances or the seven awakening factors and discern the causative and resultant formations of mentality and materiality. Discerning these formations by the five aggregates, twelve bases, the truths and similar schemes also develops contemplation of phenomena. A meditator wishing to apprehend mentality led by feeling, knowing consciousness, or contact…

M04-body-P243.title: Three points to remember about practising the foundations

paragraphs.M04-body-P243-S01: … should apprehend together the supporting materiality and the material object of that mentality. After apprehending mentality, apprehend the supporting materiality again so that mentality and materiality are apprehended together. This was explained repeatedly above.
paragraphs.M04-body-P243-S02: 1. Developing one foundation of mindfulness is called developing all four. 2. Discerning the five aggregates thoroughly by the three kinds of full understanding is developing the foundations. 3. If the five aggregates of mentality and materiality have yet to be apprehended down to ultimate reality and discerned together with their conditions according to the three characteristics, that practice does not yet constitute developing all four foundations. Those who earnestly seek the true Dhamma and aspire to Nibbāna should remember these three points with care.
paragraphs.M04-body-P243-S03: Consciousness in processes and consciousness outside processes are summarized here for ease of recollection.

M04-body-P244.title: In the seen, only the seen

paragraphs.M04-body-P244-S01:
Tasmātiha te, Bāhiya, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ: diṭṭhe diṭṭhamattaṃ bhavissati, sute sutamattaṃ bhavissati, mute mutamattaṃ bhavissati, viññāte viññātamattaṃ bhavissatīti.
Bāhiya, train in this way: in the seen there will be only the seen, in the heard only the heard, in the sensed only the sensed, and in the cognized only the cognized (Udāna, p. 85).
paragraphs.M04-body-P244-S02: The Buddha taught this practice in the Māluṅkyaputta Sutta (Saṃyutta Nikāya, vol. 2, p. 94) and the Bāhiya Sutta (Udāna, p. 85). Its meaning is as follows.
paragraphs.M04-body-P244-S03:
Ettha hi rūpāyatanaṃ passitabbaṭṭhena diṭṭhaṃ nāma, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ pana saddhiṃ taṃdvārikaviññāṇehi dassanaṭṭhena. Tadubhayampi yathāpaccayaṃ pavattamānaṃ dhammamattameva, na ettha koci kattā vā kāretā vā. Yato taṃ hutvā abhāvaṭṭhena aniccaṃ, udayabbayappaṭipīḷanaṭṭhena dukkhaṃ, avasavattanaṭṭhena anattāti, kuto tattha paṇḍitassa rajjanādīnaṃ okāsoti? Ayamettha adhippāyo sutādīsupi.
The explanation calls the visible-form base “the seen” because it is what is to be seen. It also calls eye-consciousness and consciousnesses in the eye-door and subsequent mind-door processes taking that object “the seen” in the sense that they see visible form. They proceed according to conditions. No one does it or makes them do it. Seen in terms of arising and passing away and their independence of anyone’s will, they are impermanent, suffering and non-self. Understand the heard and the remaining kinds similarly (Udāna Commentary, p. 152).
paragraphs.M04-body-P244-S04: Meditators should apprehend: 1. Visible form that is seen and eye-door and mind-door mentality that sees it. 2. Sound that is heard and ear-door and mind-door mentality that hears it…

M04-body-P245.title: The seen, heard, sensed and cognized as objects of insight

paragraphs.M04-body-P245-S01: 3. Odours, tastes and tangibles that are sensed, and the mentality of nose-door, tongue-door, body-door and corresponding mind-door processes that senses them. 4. Mind objects that are cognized and mind-door mentality that cognizes them.
paragraphs.M04-body-P245-S02: First apprehend that mentality and materiality. Then seek the causes that bring them about, such as ignorance, craving, clinging, formations and kamma, and discern deeply the seen, heard, sensed and cognized together with their causes by the three characteristics. When one practises this way, greed, hatred and delusion have no opportunity to arise on account of those objects. Instead, mind-door process series with great wholesome insight impulsion arise continuously. When insight knowledge develops to the noble path, the practice of “in the seen, only the seen” is fulfilled.
paragraphs.M04-body-P245-S03: Some teachers say, “When seeing, keep the mind only at seeing. Do not let other consciousnesses arise further on that object.” This point calls for further explanation.
paragraphs.M04-body-P245-S04:
Ettha pana cakkhuviññāṇameva dassanakiccaṃ sādheti.
Here eye-consciousness alone accomplishes the function of seeing visible form (Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 1, p. 130).

M04-body-P246.title: Eye-consciousness sees and the process continues according to conditions

paragraphs.M04-body-P246-S01: If “keep the mind only at seeing” is understood to mean allowing only eye-consciousness to arise with visible form as object and preventing other process consciousnesses from arising, the question is whether a disciple can train to make that happen. The commentary explains as follows.
paragraphs.M04-body-P246-S02:
Sace pana bhavaṅgaṃ āvaṭṭeti, kiriyāmanodhātuyā bhavaṅge āvaṭṭite voṭṭhabbanaṃ appāpetvā antarā cakkhuviññāṇe vā sampaṭicchane vā santīraṇe vā ṭhatvā nivattissatīti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Voṭṭhabbanavasena pana ṭhatvā ekaṃ vā dve vā tīṇi vā cittāni vattanti.
If the life-continuum has been turned and interrupted by five-door adverting, the functional mind-element, the process cannot stop at eye-consciousness, receiving or investigating and return to life-continuum before reaching determining. Determining consciousness can arise once, twice or three times to perform the function of determining the object (Abhidhamma Commentary, vol. 1, pp. 129–130).
paragraphs.M04-body-P246-S03: Here the commentary uses a slight-object process as an example. When visible form impinges, or appears before the eye-door and mind-door, a slight object must reach determining, a great object impulsion, and a very great object registration. The process cannot stop midway before those points. Understand similarly for heard and sensed objects. An object appearing at the mind-door…

M04-body-P247.title: Where a process ends and what “only” means

paragraphs.M04-body-P247-S01: … if indistinct cannot stop before impulsion, and if clear cannot stop before registration. With objects appearing at the two corresponding doors: 1. A slight object reaches determining. 2. A great object reaches impulsion. 3. A very great object reaches registration. At the mind-door: 1. A clear object reaches registration. 2. An indistinct object reaches impulsion. Only then does the process return to life-continuum.
paragraphs.M04-body-P247-S02: Therefore train in “in the seen only the seen”, “in the heard only the heard”, “in the sensed only the sensed”, and “in the cognized only the cognized”. These words do not mean letting only eye-consciousness arise when seeing, only ear-consciousness when hearing, or only nose-, tongue-, or body-consciousness when sensing, and training to suppress the subsequent process consciousnesses. Their meaning is…

M04-body-P248.title: The meaning for practice and closing aspiration

paragraphs.M04-body-P248-S01: 1. The phenomena seen and the phenomena that see. 2. The phenomena heard and the phenomena that hear. 3. The phenomena sensed and the phenomena that sense. 4. The phenomena cognized and the phenomena that cognize. Having apprehended and distinguished them by wisdom, seek their causes and discern deeply the seen, heard, sensed and cognized together with their causes by the three characteristics. Remember this as the main point. It is an instruction for practising so that greed, hatred and delusion do not arise in relation to the seen, heard, sensed and cognized.
paragraphs.M04-body-P248-S02: May you practise diligently and realize Nibbāna for yourselves in this very life, making full use of the opportunity to encounter the Buddha’s dispensation and following in the footsteps of arahants such as Venerable Bāhiya Dārucīriya and Venerable Māluṅkyaputta…
paragraphs.M04-body-P248-S03:
Pa-Auk Tawya Sayadaw
Cittalapabbata Monastery, Pa-Auk Tawya
Myanmar Era 1367.
